  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.1  The First 5 Minutes — The Setup Ritual                            🎯
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Before you touch a single question, invest 5 minutes building your tooling.
  This pays back minutes on EVERY task afterward. Set up four things: the k alias
  + completion, the $do / $now exports, a YAML-safe vim, and your doc bookmarks.

      # ~/.bashrc  (then load it:  source ~/.bashrc )
      alias k=kubectl
      source <(kubectl completion bash)
      complete -o default -F __start_kubectl k     # completion works on `k` too
      export do="--dry-run=client -o yaml"          # k create deploy x $do > x.yaml
      export now="--force --grace-period=0"         # k delete pod x $now (fast)
      alias kgp='kubectl get pods -o wide'
      alias kn='kubectl config set-context --current --namespace'

      # ~/.vimrc
      set tabstop=2 shiftwidth=2 expandtab
      set number autoindent
      " paste-safe YAML: type  :set paste  BEFORE pasting indented blocks

  💡 INSIGHT: $do is the single highest-leverage export — it turns any imperative
  `create` into a perfectly-indented YAML scaffold you can edit, eliminating the
  #1 source of lost points (indentation errors).

  ⚠️ GOTCHA: in vim, pasting a YAML block without `:set paste` cascades the
  autoindent and corrupts the indentation. Toggle it before every paste.

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.1b  Verify Env Each Task — Context & Namespace                       🎯
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  The exam switches CLUSTERS per question. Each task tells you which context to
  use. ALWAYS start a task by switching context and setting the namespace —
  otherwise you will do flawless work in the wrong cluster and score zero.

      kubectl config get-contexts                  # list what's available
      kubectl config use-context <context>         # the task gives you this line
      kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=<ns>

  🔑 MUST-REMEMBER: The first command of every question is `use-context`. Copy
  the exact context string from the question prompt — do not type it from memory.


  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.2  The 3-Pass Time Strategy                                          🎯
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Do NOT solve questions in order. Triage them into three passes by effort, so
  you bank guaranteed points first and never let one hard task eat your exam.

   ┌──────────────── THE 120-MINUTE BATTLE PLAN ────────────────┐
   │ maximize POINTS PER MINUTE, not perfection                 │
   │                                                            │
   │ ⚡ Setup  (5m)  ████  aliases · completion · vim · bookmarks │
   │ 🟢 Pass 1 (35m) ████████████        every task < 4 min      │
   │                  (quick wins — banked points)              │
   │ 🟡 Pass 2 (50m) ██████████████████  5–8 min tasks           │
   │                  (the BULK of your score)                  │
   │ 🔴 Pass 3 (30m) ██████████          hardest + VERIFY all    │
   │                                                            │
   │ Rules:  switch CONTEXT every question · generate YAML with │
   │ $do · NEVER camp >10 min on one task · 66% to pass ·       │
   │ NEVER leave a question blank (partial credit is real).     │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Pass 1 (≈35m): Read every question once. Solve everything you can finish in
  under 4 minutes — RBAC creates, expose a Service, scale a Deployment, a taint,
  a label. Flag the rest.

  Pass 2 (≈50m): The 5–8 minute tasks — most of your score lives here. Ingress,
  NetworkPolicy, PVC + mount, HPA, rolling update. Generate YAML, adjust, verify.

  Pass 3 (≈30m): The hardest tasks (etcd restore, kubeadm upgrade, multi-step
  troubleshooting) and a final VERIFY sweep across everything you answered.

  ⚡ SPEED TIP: A 4% question and a 13% question both deserve the same 4-minute
  effort in Pass 1. Don't over-invest in low-weight tasks — read the weight.

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.3  Imperative vs Declarative on the Clock                            🧭
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Speed comes from imperative commands; correctness on complex objects comes from
  declarative YAML generated by those commands. Use this decision guide:

   🧭 DECISION GUIDE — how to produce the object
   ┌────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Need                       │ Fastest correct path                          │
   ├────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   │ Pod / Deployment / Job     │ k create … $do > x.yaml  → edit → apply       │
   │ Service (expose)           │ k expose … (pure imperative, no YAML)         │
   │ RBAC (sa/role/binding)     │ k create sa|role|rolebinding … (imperative)   │
   │ ConfigMap / Secret         │ k create cm|secret … --from-literal           │
   │ NetworkPolicy / Ingress    │ COPY skeleton from kubernetes.io docs → edit  │
   │ Gateway API HTTPRoute      │ COPY skeleton from docs → edit                │
   │ Field name you forgot      │ kubectl explain <kind>.spec --recursive       │
   └────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  💡 INSIGHT: NetworkPolicy, Ingress and Gateway API are too fiddly to author
  from memory. The exam ALLOWS kubernetes.io/docs — copy a known-good skeleton
  and adjust selectors/ports. Adjusting beats authoring, every time.

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.4  Domain-by-Domain Strategy                                         🎯
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  How to attack each of the five weighted domains, with the command kit per
  domain. Drill these until they are reflexive.

   ┌─ Cluster Architecture / Install (25%) ─────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ RBAC: k create sa|role|clusterrole|rolebinding|clusterrolebinding …        │
   │ kubeadm upgrade: drain → apt upgrade kubeadm → kubeadm upgrade apply →     │
   │   upgrade kubelet/kubectl → uncordon (control plane first, then workers).  │
   │ etcd: etcdctl snapshot save/restore (with --cacert/--cert/--key).          │
   │ Static pods: drop YAML in /etc/kubernetes/manifests; kubelet auto-runs it. │
   │ CSR: kubectl get csr → kubectl certificate approve <name>.                 │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   ┌─ Workloads & Scheduling (15%) ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ k set image / k rollout undo (rolling update + rollback).                  │
   │ k autoscale deploy … --min --max --cpu-percent (HPA).                      │
   │ k taint nodes / tolerations + nodeSelector / affinity for placement.       │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   ┌─ Services & Networking (20%) ──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ k expose … --type=NodePort|ClusterIP --port --target-port.                 │
   │ NetworkPolicy default-deny + allow (copy from docs).                       │
   │ Ingress / Gateway API HTTPRoute (copy from docs, set host/path/backend).   │
   │ DNS debug: kubectl run tmp --image=busybox -it --rm -- nslookup <svc>.     │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   ┌─ Storage (10%) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ PVC referencing a StorageClass (dynamic provisioning).                     │
   │ Mount the PVC: volumes[].persistentVolumeClaim + volumeMounts in the pod.  │
   │ Check binding: kubectl get pvc,pv ; describe pvc for the events.           │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   ┌─ Troubleshooting (30% — the biggest slice) ────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Node NotReady: ssh node → systemctl status/restart kubelet → journalctl.   │
   │ CrashLoop: kubectl logs --previous ; describe for the last state/reason.   │
   │ Service no endpoints: selector vs pod labels + readiness.                  │
   │ DNS: check CoreDNS pods/Service; nslookup from a temp pod.                  │
   │ PVC Pending: StorageClass exists? provisioner running? access mode match?  │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  🔑 MUST-REMEMBER: 30% of the exam is troubleshooting — `describe`, `logs
  --previous`, `events`, and `journalctl -u kubelet` are your four scalpels.

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.5  Top 10 Point-Losers                                               ⚠️
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   1.  Working in the WRONG context/namespace (correct work, zero score).
   2.  Typos in resource names/labels (auto-grader matches exact strings).
   3.  YAML indentation errors from hand-writing instead of generating.
   4.  Not VERIFYING (silent failure you never see).
   5.  Hand-writing YAML you could have generated with $do.
   6.  Forgetting $now on deletes — pods stuck Terminating eat your clock.
   7.  etcd RESTORE in the wrong order (restore to new data-dir, repoint, verify).
   8.  Deprecated API versions (e.g. extensions/v1beta1) — use current apps/v1.
   9.  Camping >10 min on one task while easy points go untouched.
   10. Leaving a question BLANK — partial credit means a best effort beats zero.

   ┌──────────────── POINT-LOSER → FIX (memorize this) ─────────────────┐
   │ wrong context      → use-context FIRST, every task                 │
   │ typos              → tab-complete + copy names from the prompt     │
   │ indentation        → $do generates it; :set paste in vim           │
   │ no verify          → get -o wide · describe · curl after each task │
   │ stuck >10 min      → flag, partial answer, move on, return Pass 3  │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.6  Scoring & Partial Credit                                          🎯
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  • Tasks are WEIGHTED (a multi-step task is worth more than a one-liner) and the
    weight is shown on each question — let it set your effort.
  • Grading is AUTOMATED against live cluster state: exact names, namespaces and
    labels matter because a script reads the object, not a human reading intent.
  • PARTIAL CREDIT is real: a task with three checks can earn 2/3 even if the
    last step fails. Always leave a best-effort answer.
  • You need 66% to pass. Aim to bank ~75% of available points and verify the
    rest — you do not need a perfect score.

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

   BEFORE:  government photo ID ready · clean desk, no notes · webcam room scan ·

            one external monitor max per current policy — confirm the rules.
   DURING:  run the setup ritual first · switch CONTEXT every question · use the
            allowed kubernetes.io docs (one extra browser tab) · 3-pass strategy ·
            flag-and-return; never blank · verify after every task.
   AFTER:   results typically within 24 hours by email · ONE free retake included ·

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45.8  THE SIMULATOR — 20 Timed Performance Tasks on easypj           🧪🎯
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Twenty performance tasks weighted to the real domains, all on the easypj
  project (Django PROJECT) / jobpost (Django APP) running on Kubernetes with
  PostgreSQL. Set a 120-minute clock, apply the 3-pass strategy, then self-score.
  Each task carries a Show Answer (the fast path) and a Show Explanation.

   ── Cluster Architecture & Installation (25%) ───────────────────────────────

   H1 · RBAC — SA + Role + Binding
       TASK: In ns easypj, create ServiceAccount jobpost-reader that can
             get/list/watch pods. Verify.
       ANSWER:
         k create sa jobpost-reader -n easypj
         k create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods -n easypj
         k create rolebinding jobpost-reader-rb --role=pod-reader \
           --serviceaccount=easypj:jobpost-reader -n easypj
         k auth can-i list pods -n easypj \
           --as=system:serviceaccount:easypj:jobpost-reader
       WHY: All three pieces are imperative — no YAML to hand-write. The
            auth can-i --as check proves the binding before you move on.

   H2 · kubeadm Cluster Upgrade
       TASK: Upgrade the control-plane node from the current minor to the next.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl drain <cp> --ignore-daemonsets
         apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubeadm=<ver>
         kubeadm upgrade plan && kubeadm upgrade apply v<ver>
         apt-get install -y kubelet=<ver> kubectl=<ver>
         systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
         kubectl uncordon <cp>
       WHY: Order matters — drain, upgrade kubeadm, apply, THEN upgrade
            kubelet/kubectl, then uncordon. Control plane before workers.

   H3 · etcd Backup + Restore
       TASK: Snapshot etcd, then restore it to a new data directory.
       ANSWER:
         ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /opt/snap.db \
           --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
           --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
           --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key
         etcdctl snapshot status /opt/snap.db
         etcdctl snapshot restore /opt/snap.db --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-new
         # edit /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml → point hostPath to etcd-new
       WHY: Restore to a NEW dir, repoint the static-pod manifest, let kubelet
            restart etcd, then verify objects return. Never restore over a live dir.

   H4 · Static Pod
       TASK: Schedule a static pod jobpost-cache on a node via the kubelet.
       ANSWER:
         k run jobpost-cache --image=redis:7 $do > /tmp/p.yaml
         # copy to the NODE:  /etc/kubernetes/manifests/jobpost-cache.yaml
         # kubelet auto-creates it; name gets "-<node>" suffix on the API server
       WHY: Static pods are owned by the kubelet, not the scheduler — placing
            the manifest in the manifests dir is the whole job.

   H5 · Approve a CSR
       TASK: A new user submitted a CertificateSigningRequest; approve it.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl get csr
         kubectl certificate approve <csr-name>
         kubectl get csr <csr-name>   # Condition: Approved,Issued
       WHY: One command to approve; verify the condition flips to Issued.

   ── Workloads & Scheduling (15%) ─────────────────────────────────────────────

   H6 · Rolling Update + Rollback
       TASK: Update Deployment easypj-web to image easypj:v2, then roll back.
       ANSWER:
         k set image deploy/easypj-web easypj=easypj:v2 -n easypj
         k rollout status deploy/easypj-web -n easypj
         k rollout undo deploy/easypj-web -n easypj
       WHY: set image triggers the rolling update; rollout undo reverts to the
            previous ReplicaSet. rollout history shows revisions.

   H7 · HorizontalPodAutoscaler
       TASK: Autoscale easypj-web 2→10 replicas at 70% CPU.
       ANSWER:
         k autoscale deploy easypj-web --min=2 --max=10 --cpu-percent=70 -n easypj
         k get hpa -n easypj
       WHY: Requires resource requests on the pod + metrics-server running, or
            the HPA shows <unknown> for current CPU.

   H8 · Taint + Toleration
       TASK: Taint a node tier=db:NoSchedule and let the postgres pod tolerate it.
       ANSWER:
         k taint nodes <node> tier=db:NoSchedule
         # in the pod spec:
         #   tolerations:
         #   - key: tier
         #     operator: Equal
         #     value: db
         #     effect: NoSchedule
       WHY: The taint repels everything; only the matching toleration lets the
            postgres pod land there.

   ── Services & Networking (20%) ──────────────────────────────────────────────

   H9 · Expose via NodePort
       TASK: Expose Deployment easypj-web on NodePort, port 80→8000.
       ANSWER:
         k expose deploy easypj-web --type=NodePort --port=80 --target-port=8000 \
           -n easypj
         k get svc easypj-web -n easypj   # note the 3xxxx NodePort
       WHY: Pure imperative — no YAML needed. Verify the allocated nodePort.

   H10 · NetworkPolicy default-deny
       TASK: In ns easypj, deny all ingress, then allow only from jobpost-web.
       ANSWER (copy the default-deny + allow skeleton from docs):
         # default-deny-ingress: podSelector: {} ; policyTypes: [Ingress]
         # allow: from: podSelector matchLabels app=jobpost-web
       WHY: Start with empty podSelector default-deny, then layer an allow.
            Copy from kubernetes.io — don't author from memory.

   H11 · Ingress
       TASK: Route easypj.local/ to the easypj-web Service.
       ANSWER (copy Ingress skeleton from docs):
         # host: easypj.local · path: / (Prefix) · backend: svc easypj-web:80
         k get ingress -n easypj
       WHY: Needs an ingress controller running; set ingressClassName and the
            backend service/port.

   H12 · Gateway API HTTPRoute
       TASK: Add an HTTPRoute sending /jobs to the jobpost Service.
       ANSWER (copy HTTPRoute skeleton from docs):
         # parentRefs: <gateway> · rules: matches path /jobs · backendRefs jobpost:80
       WHY: Gateway API is in the 2025 syllabus — HTTPRoute attaches to a
            Gateway via parentRefs. Copy the skeleton and edit.

   ── Storage (10%) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

   H13 · Dynamic PVC
       TASK: Create a 1Gi PVC easypj-data using the default StorageClass.
       ANSWER:
         # PVC: accessModes [ReadWriteOnce] · resources.requests.storage 1Gi
         k get pvc easypj-data -n easypj   # should reach Bound
       WHY: With a default StorageClass + provisioner, the PVC binds
            automatically to a freshly-provisioned PV.

   H14 · Mount PVC in a Pod
       TASK: Mount easypj-data at /var/lib/postgresql/data in the postgres pod.
       ANSWER:
         # spec.volumes: - name: data ; persistentVolumeClaim.claimName easypj-data
         # container.volumeMounts: - name: data ; mountPath /var/lib/postgresql/data
       WHY: Two stanzas must agree on the volume NAME — volumes[] and
            volumeMounts[] are joined by it.

   ── Troubleshooting (30% — the biggest slice) ────────────────────────────────

   H15 · Node NotReady
       TASK: A worker shows NotReady; bring it back.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl get nodes ; kubectl describe node <n>
         ssh <node> ; systemctl status kubelet ; systemctl restart kubelet
         journalctl -u kubelet -f
       WHY: NotReady is almost always a dead/mis-configured kubelet — restart
            and read its journal for the real cause.

   H16 · CrashLoopBackOff
       TASK: The easypj-web pod is CrashLooping; find and fix the cause.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl logs <pod> -n easypj --previous
         kubectl describe pod <pod> -n easypj   # Last State / Reason / exit code
       WHY: --previous reads the logs of the crashed container; describe shows
            the exit reason (bad env, missing config, OOMKilled).

   H17 · Service with No Endpoints
       TASK: easypj-web Service returns nothing; no endpoints listed.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl get endpointslices -n easypj
         kubectl get svc easypj-web -o yaml   # selector
         kubectl get pods --show-labels -n easypj
       WHY: Align the Service SELECTOR with the pods' LABELS and make sure pods
            are Ready — only ready pods populate the EndpointSlice.

   H18 · DNS Resolution
       TASK: Pods can't resolve easypj-web.easypj.svc.cluster.local.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns
         kubectl run tmp --image=busybox:1.36 -it --rm --restart=Never -- \
           nslookup easypj-web.easypj
       WHY: Check CoreDNS is Running, then test resolution from a throwaway pod.

   H19 · PVC Pending
       TASK: easypj-data PVC is stuck Pending.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl describe pvc easypj-data -n easypj    # events explain it
         kubectl get storageclass
       WHY: Pending = no StorageClass / no provisioner / access-mode mismatch.
            The describe events name the exact reason.

   H20 · Broken kubeconfig
       TASK: kubectl can't reach the cluster — fix the kubeconfig.
       ANSWER:
         kubectl config view ; kubectl cluster-info
         # fix server URL / cluster CA / context's user; use-context the right one
       WHY: Usually a wrong server address, stale cert, or the context points at
            the wrong cluster/user.

   ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   SCORING:  Target 20 tasks in <120 minutes, self-scored.  75%+ = you are ready
   to book the exam.  Below 75% → drill the domains where you lost points and re-run.

  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🔧 UNDER-THE-HOOD / 🔬 DEEPER — Chapter 45
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🔧 HOW TASKS ARE AUTO-GRADED: each question runs a server-side script after you
     submit; it queries live cluster state (e.g. "does ns easypj have a
     ServiceAccount named jobpost-reader bound to a role granting list pods?").
     It matches EXACT names, namespaces, labels and field values — which is why a
     typo or wrong namespace scores zero even when your intent was perfect, and
     why partial-credit checks are independent (you can pass 2 of 3 sub-checks).

  🔬 DEEPER (exam + beyond):
   • PSI remote-desktop quirks: the exam runs in a remote Linux desktop inside the
     PSI Secure Browser. Copy/paste uses Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V in the
     terminal; a notepad widget is provided for scratch. Practice the latency.
   • killer.sh: your two included sessions are HARDER than the real exam by design
     — treat a 60–70% there as a healthy real-exam score. Re-read every solution.
   • tmux: split panes so you can watch `kubectl get … -w` in one pane while you
     edit YAML in another; it survives if the SSH-into-node session drops.
   • vimrc for YAML: 2-space expandtab + autoindent + `:set paste` is the
     difference between clean YAML and a cascade of indentation errors.
   • Fast ctx/ns: `kubectl config use-context` then `kn <ns>` (the alias) at the
     top of every task — make it reflex, not a decision.
   • Docs-search workflow: keep ONE allowed kubernetes.io tab; use its search for
     "networkpolicy", "ingress", "gateway httproute", "volumes" and copy the
     example block straight into vim, then edit selectors/ports.
   • Flagging: the exam lets you flag/skip; pair it with the 3-pass plan so flagged
     items are exactly your Pass-3 backlog.
   • 2025 syllabus deltas to drill: Gateway API (HTTPRoute), CRDs/Operators
     awareness, Helm/Kustomize basics, and the heavier 30% troubleshooting slice —
     these are the newest, most under-practiced points.

  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🔑 KEY TAKEAWAYS — Chapter 45
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  • The CKA is a 2-hour, hands-on SPEED + ACCURACY test (66% to pass). Most
    failures are time/process, not knowledge.
  • Spend the first 5 minutes on the setup ritual: k alias + completion, $do
    (dry-run YAML) + $now (fast delete), vim 2-space expandtab, doc bookmarks.
  • Work 3 passes: quick wins (<4m) → medium (5–8m) → hardest + verify. Never
    camp >10 min on one task; never leave a question blank (partial credit).
  • Switch CONTEXT/namespace every question, generate YAML instead of hand-writing
    it, copy NetworkPolicy/Ingress/Gateway skeletons from the docs, and VERIFY
    after every task.
  • Grading is automated against live cluster state — exact names, namespaces and
    labels are non-negotiable.
  • The simulator on easypj is your readiness gate: 75%+ = book the exam.

  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  ⚠️ GOTCHAS — Chapter 45
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  • Skipping the setup ritual costs minutes on every single task afterward.
  • Forgetting `kubectl config use-context` (or the namespace) → you do correct
    work in the WRONG cluster and score zero.
  • Perfectionism: polishing one task while three easy ones go untouched.
  • Hand-writing YAML (typos/indentation) instead of generating it with $do.
  • Forgetting $now on deletes, or using deprecated API versions
    (extensions/v1beta1 instead of apps/v1).
  • Pasting YAML into vim without `:set paste` corrupts the indentation.
  • etcd restore done over the live data-dir instead of a fresh one, or without
    repointing the static-pod manifest afterward.

  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  ⚡ SPEED TIPS — Chapter 45
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  • `k create deploy easypj-web --image=easypj:v1 $do > d.yaml` then edit — far
    faster and safer than writing from scratch.
  • Bookmark kubernetes.io/docs for NetworkPolicy, Ingress, and Gateway API —
    copy-paste-adjust beats memorizing YAML.
  • Verify with the same command set every time: get -o wide, describe, auth
    can-i, and a curl from a temp pod.
  • `kubectl explain <kind>.spec --recursive | less` finds a forgotten field
    without leaving the terminal.
  • `k delete pod x $now` clears a stuck-Terminating pod instantly.
  • Match the weight: don't spend 8 minutes on a 4% task in Pass 1.

  🔑 COMMANDS — Chapter 45 (the exam alias / dry-run kit)
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   alias k=kubectl ; source <(kubectl completion bash) ; complete -F __start_kubectl k
   export do='--dry-run=client -o yaml' ; export now='--force --grace-period=0'
   kubectl config get-contexts ; kubectl config use-context <c>
   kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=<ns>
   k create deploy web --image=nginx $do > web.yaml ; k apply -f web.yaml
   k expose deploy web --type=NodePort --port=80 --target-port=8000
   k create sa <name> -n <ns>
   k create role r --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods -n <ns>
   k create rolebinding rb --role=r --serviceaccount=<ns>:<sa> -n <ns>
   k auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> -n <ns>
   k set image deploy/<d> <c>=<img>:<tag> ; k rollout status|undo deploy/<d>
   k autoscale deploy <d> --min=2 --max=10 --cpu-percent=70
   ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save|restore … --cacert --cert --key
   kubectl logs <pod> --previous ; kubectl describe pod <pod>
   kubectl get endpointslices ; kubectl get pods --show-labels
   journalctl -u kubelet -f ; systemctl restart kubelet
   kubectl explain <kind>.spec --recursive | less     # field lookup, no docs

  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🧪 LAB Q&A — Chapter 45 (10) — full answer + explanation each
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   Q1. First thing you do when the exam starts?
       A. The setup ritual: k alias + bash completion, $do/$now exports, vim
          config (2-space expandtab), doc bookmarks, and confirm the current
          context. It pays back time on every task afterward.

   Q2. How do you avoid working in the wrong cluster?
       A. Run `kubectl config use-context <c>` (and set the namespace) at the
          START of every question — the exam switches clusters per task, and the
          auto-grader reads the cluster you were told to use.

   Q3. Outline the 3-pass time strategy.
       A. Pass 1: all <4-min quick wins (banked points). Pass 2: 5–8-min tasks
          (the bulk of your score). Pass 3: hardest tasks + verify everything.
          Never spend >10 min on one task.

   Q4. Create a Deployment fast without writing YAML by hand.
       A. `k create deploy easypj-web --image=easypj:v1 $do > d.yaml`, edit the
          file, then `k apply -f d.yaml`. $do generates perfectly-indented YAML.

   Q5. RBAC task: SA + Role + Binding to read pods. Fast path?
       A. `k create sa web -n easypj`; `k create role r --verb=get,list,watch
          --resource=pods -n easypj`; `k create rolebinding rb --role=r
          --serviceaccount=easypj:web -n easypj`; verify with
          `k auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:easypj:web -n easypj`.

   Q6. etcd backup+restore — the must-not-miss order?
       A. snapshot save (with certs) → verify status → restore to a NEW data-dir
          → repoint the etcd static-pod manifest → verify objects return. Never
          restore over the live data directory.

   Q7. A Service has no endpoints in a troubleshooting task. Fix approach?
       A. Compare the Service selector to the pods' labels and check readiness;
          align them so ready pods populate the EndpointSlice. Use
          `kubectl get pods --show-labels` and the Service's selector to diff.

   Q8. How do you handle a task you can't finish in 10 minutes?
       A. Flag it, leave a best-effort partial answer (partial credit is real),
          move on, and return in Pass 3 if time remains — never leave it blank.

   Q9. Why generate YAML and copy policy/ingress skeletons from docs?
       A. To avoid indentation/typo errors and save time; the exam allows the
          kubernetes.io docs — adjust a known-good template instead of authoring
          NetworkPolicy/Ingress/Gateway from memory.

   Q10. What's the single highest-value habit during the exam?
       A. Verify after EVERY task (get/describe/curl/auth can-i) so you never lose
          points to a silent mistake — accuracy compounds across 15–20 tasks.

  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  🧭 VISUAL SUMMARY — Chapter 45: the exam battle plan on one page
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   ┌──────────────────────────── KEY TAKEAWAYS ─────────────────────────────────┐
   │ ✅ Spend the first 5 minutes on aliases/completion/vim/bookmarks.          │
   │ ✅ 3 passes: quick wins → medium → hard; never camp on one task; never     │
   │    leave a question blank (partial credit is real).                        │
   │ ✅ Switch context EVERY question; verify after EVERY task; generate YAML.  │
   │ ✅ 66% to pass — maximize points/minute, not perfection.                   │
   │ 🎯 The simulator on easypj is your readiness gate: 75%+ = book the exam.   │
   │ 🔑 k · $do · $now · config use-context · auth can-i · explain              │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

   .vs-prose — In words: the CKA is won by PROCESS, not just knowledge. Open with
   the 5-minute setup ritual (k alias, completion, $do/$now, vim 2-space, doc
   bookmarks). Switch context at the top of every question so your work lands in
   the right cluster. Triage in three passes — bank the <4-minute quick wins,
   then the 5–8-minute middle that holds most of your score, then the hardest
   tasks plus a verify sweep — never camping past 10 minutes and never leaving a
   blank, because partial credit rewards a best effort. Generate YAML with $do,
   copy NetworkPolicy/Ingress/Gateway skeletons from the allowed docs, and verify
   with get/describe/curl/auth-can-i after every task. Drill the 20-task easypj
   simulator under a 120-minute clock; clear 75% and you are ready to book —
   setup → 3 passes → verify → pass.
