================================================================================
  Appendix A: kubectl Admin Command Reference
================================================================================

  📖 META: One-stop kubectl operator reference. Every block is verbatim-runnable.
  🎯 EXAM: ~70% of CKA tasks start with a kubectl command from this appendix.
  🔑 MUST-REMEMBER: `export do='--dry-run=client -o yaml'` then `kubectl create
     ... $do > file.yaml` is the fastest path to a manifest — see A.9.

  SECTION MAP
    A.1  Cluster Management Commands
    A.2  Node Management
    A.3  Workload Commands
    A.4  Debugging Commands
    A.5  RBAC Commands
    A.6  Certificate Commands
    A.7  etcd Commands
    A.8  Helm & Kustomize
    A.9  Speed Kit (aliases, $do, $now, completion, jsonpath snippets)


  A.1  Cluster Management Commands
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ kubectl cluster-info
       $ kubectl cluster-info dump                     # full diagnostic dump
       $ kubectl get componentstatuses                 # (deprecated, still asked)
       $ kubectl top nodes
       $ kubectl top pods --all-namespaces
       $ kubectl get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
       $ kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
       $ kubectl api-resources                         # all kinds + short names
       $ kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true       # only namespaced kinds
       $ kubectl api-versions                          # all served group/versions
       $ kubectl version --short                       # client + server versions
       $ kubectl config view --minify                  # current context only

  💡 `kubectl api-resources` is the fastest way to recall a short name (e.g.
     deploy, svc, ns, sa, netpol, pvc) and whether a kind is namespaced.


  A.2  Node Management
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ kubectl get nodes -o wide
       $ kubectl describe node <name>
       $ kubectl cordon <node>                         # mark unschedulable
       $ kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
       $ kubectl uncordon <node>                       # re-enable scheduling
       $ kubectl taint nodes <node> key=value:NoSchedule
       $ kubectl taint nodes <node> key=value:NoSchedule-      # remove (trailing -)
       $ kubectl label nodes <node> disk=ssd
       $ kubectl label nodes <node> disk-              # remove label
       $ kubectl get node <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.capacity}'

  ⚠️ GOTCHA: `drain` fails on bare pods and on pods not backed by a controller
     unless you add `--force`. DaemonSet pods always need `--ignore-daemonsets`.
     Drain implicitly cordons first; uncordon does NOT reschedule evicted pods —
     controllers do that.

  🧭 cordon vs drain
       cordon = "no NEW pods here" (existing pods stay)
       drain  = cordon + evict existing pods gracefully (for maintenance/upgrade)


  A.3  Workload Commands
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ kubectl create deployment <name> --image=<image> --replicas=3
       $ kubectl scale deployment <name> --replicas=5
       $ kubectl autoscale deployment <name> --min=2 --max=10 --cpu-percent=80
       $ kubectl rollout status deployment <name>
       $ kubectl rollout history deployment <name>
       $ kubectl rollout history deployment <name> --revision=2
       $ kubectl rollout undo deployment <name>
       $ kubectl rollout undo deployment <name> --to-revision=2
       $ kubectl rollout restart deployment <name>     # roll all pods, same image
       $ kubectl rollout pause deployment <name>
       $ kubectl rollout resume deployment <name>
       $ kubectl set image deployment/<name> container=image:tag
       $ kubectl set resources deployment/<name> --limits=cpu=500m,memory=256Mi

  Example (the running app):
       $ kubectl create deployment jobpost --image=easypj/jobpost:1.0 --replicas=3
       $ kubectl set image deployment/jobpost jobpost=easypj/jobpost:1.1
       $ kubectl rollout status deployment/jobpost


  A.4  Debugging Commands
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ kubectl describe pod <name>
       $ kubectl logs <pod> [--previous] [-c container] [-f] [--tail=N]
       $ kubectl logs <pod> -p                          # previous container (crash)
       $ kubectl logs -l app=jobpost --all-containers    # by label, all containers
       $ kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /bin/sh
       $ kubectl exec <pod> -c <container> -- env        # one-shot command
       $ kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox --target=<container>   # ephemeral
       $ kubectl debug node/<node> -it --image=busybox  # node debug pod
       $ kubectl port-forward <pod> local:container
       $ kubectl port-forward svc/jobpost 8080:80
       $ kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=<pod>
       $ kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> [--as=user]
       $ kubectl get pod <pod> -o yaml | less           # inspect full spec/status

  🩺 First three commands on ANY broken pod:
       1) kubectl get pod <pod> -o wide      (state, node, restarts, IP)
       2) kubectl describe pod <pod>         (events at the bottom)
       3) kubectl logs <pod> [-p]            (app errors / crash reason)


  A.5  RBAC Commands
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ kubectl create role <name> --verb=get,list --resource=pods
       $ kubectl create clusterrole <name> --verb='*' --resource='*'
       $ kubectl create rolebinding <name> --role=<role> --user=<user>
       $ kubectl create rolebinding <name> --role=<role> --serviceaccount=ns:sa
       $ kubectl create clusterrolebinding <name> --clusterrole=<role> --user=<user>
       $ kubectl auth can-i --list --as=<user>
       $ kubectl auth can-i --list --as=system:serviceaccount:ns:sa
       $ kubectl auth can-i create deployments --namespace dev --as dev-user

  🧭 Role vs ClusterRole  /  RoleBinding vs ClusterRoleBinding
       Role        = permissions, single namespace
       ClusterRole = permissions, cluster-wide OR reusable across namespaces
       RoleBinding        = grant in ONE namespace (can reference a ClusterRole)
       ClusterRoleBinding = grant cluster-wide


  A.6  Certificate Commands
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ kubeadm certs check-expiration
       $ kubeadm certs renew all
       $ kubeadm certs renew apiserver                  # renew a single cert
       $ openssl x509 -in <cert> -text -noout           # decode a certificate
       $ openssl x509 -in <cert> -noout -dates          # just notBefore/notAfter
       $ openssl req -in <csr> -text -noout              # decode a CSR
       $ kubectl get csr                                 # pending CSRs
       $ kubectl certificate approve <csr-name>

  ⚠️ GOTCHA: After `kubeadm certs renew all` you must restart the static control-
     plane pods (move /etc/kubernetes/manifests aside and back, or `crictl rm`
     the kube-apiserver/controller-manager/scheduler containers) and refresh any
     copied kubeconfigs. kubelet client certs auto-rotate; admin.conf does not.


  A.7  etcd Commands
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save <file>
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore <file>
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status <file> --write-table
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl member list
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl member list --write-out=table
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint health
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table

  Required flags on a kubeadm cluster (point at the right CA + client certs):
       --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
       --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
       --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
       --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

  Full backup one-liner:
       $ ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
           --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
           --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
           --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
           snapshot save /var/lib/etcd-backup/snapshot.db

  ⚠️ GOTCHA: `snapshot restore` writes a NEW data-dir; it does not overwrite the
     live one. After restore, point etcd's static pod `--data-dir` at the new
     directory (or restore to the same path with etcd stopped) and restart the
     control plane. See Appendix E for the full runbook.


  A.8  Helm & Kustomize
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       $ helm repo add <name> <url>     &&  helm repo update
       $ helm search repo <keyword>
       $ helm install <release> <chart> -n <ns> --create-namespace
       $ helm install <release> <chart> -f values.yaml --set image.tag=1.1
       $ helm upgrade <release> <chart> --reuse-values --set replicas=3
       $ helm upgrade --install <release> <chart>       # idempotent deploy
       $ helm rollback <release> <revision>
       $ helm history <release>
       $ helm list -A
       $ helm uninstall <release> -n <ns>
       $ helm template <release> <chart>                # render, do not apply
       $ helm get manifest <release>                    # what's actually deployed

       $ kubectl apply -k ./overlays/prod               # apply a Kustomize dir
       $ kubectl kustomize ./overlays/prod              # preview rendered YAML
       $ kubectl delete -k ./overlays/prod

  🧭 Helm vs Kustomize
       Helm      = templated, versioned charts + release lifecycle (install/
                   upgrade/rollback). Best for packaged third-party apps.
       Kustomize = template-free overlays (base + patches), built into kubectl
                   (-k). Best for "same app, small per-env diffs."


  A.9  Speed Kit (aliases, $do, $now, completion, jsonpath snippets)
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ⚡ Put these at the TOP of every exam terminal — they pay for themselves in
     the first task.

       alias k=kubectl
       complete -o default -F __start_kubectl k         # tab-complete for `k`
       export do='--dry-run=client -o yaml'             # generate manifests
       export now='--force --grace-period=0'            # delete pods instantly
       export KUBE_EDITOR=vim
       source <(kubectl completion bash)

  Generate-then-edit pattern (do NOT hand-write YAML):
       $ k run nginx --image=nginx $do > pod.yaml
       $ k create deploy web --image=nginx --replicas=3 $do > deploy.yaml
       $ k create svc clusterip web --tcp=80:8080 $do > svc.yaml
       $ k delete pod nginx $now

  JSONPath / custom-columns snippets (common exam outputs):
       # all node internal IPs
       $ k get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}'
       # pod -> node mapping
       $ k get pods -o custom-columns=POD:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName
       # all images used in a namespace
       $ k get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'
       # sort pods by restart count
       $ k get pods --sort-by='.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount'
       # container ready states
       $ k get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].ready}'

  Context / namespace fast-switch:
       $ k config set-context --current --namespace=jobpost
       $ k config use-context <ctx>
       $ k config get-contexts

  ⚡ SPEED TIPS
       • Set the namespace once with `set-context --current --namespace=X`
         instead of typing `-n X` on every command.
       • `k explain pod.spec.containers --recursive` recalls any field path with
         no internet — your offline schema reference.
       • `$do` + a generator beats hand-typed YAML on both speed and accuracy.

  🔑 COMMANDS (the appendix in one screen)
       k api-resources            • k cordon/drain/uncordon NODE
       k rollout undo/restart     • k logs -p / k debug
       k auth can-i --list --as=  • kubeadm certs renew all
       etcdctl snapshot save/restore/status --write-table
       helm upgrade --install / helm rollback   • kubectl apply -k

  🧪 LAB Q&A — Appendix A
    Q1. 🟢 Generate a Deployment manifest for jobpost (3 replicas, image
        easypj/jobpost:1.0) without writing YAML by hand.
        A. k create deploy jobpost --image=easypj/jobpost:1.0 --replicas=3 \
             --dry-run=client -o yaml > jobpost.yaml   (i.e. `... $do > ...`).

    Q2. 🟡 A node must be patched. Safely move all pods off it, then return it to
        service after the reboot.
        A. kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
           ...reboot... then kubectl uncordon <node>. Drain auto-cordons first.

    Q3. 🟡 The jobpost rollout introduced a bad image. Roll back to the previous
        revision and confirm.
        A. kubectl rollout undo deployment/jobpost ;
           kubectl rollout status deployment/jobpost ;
           kubectl rollout history deployment/jobpost.

    Q4. 🟡 Prove whether service account jobpost-sa in namespace jobpost may
        create deployments.
        A. kubectl auth can-i create deployments \
             --as=system:serviceaccount:jobpost:jobpost-sa -n jobpost
           (or `--list` for the full permission set).

    Q5. 🔴 Take a verified etcd snapshot on a kubeadm control-plane node.
        A. ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
             --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
             --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
             --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
             snapshot save /var/lib/etcd-backup/snap.db ;
           then verify: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status \
             /var/lib/etcd-backup/snap.db --write-table.

    Q6. 🔴 Control-plane certs expire in 5 days. Renew them and bring the cluster
        back cleanly.
        A. kubeadm certs check-expiration ; kubeadm certs renew all ;
           restart the static control-plane pods (move
           /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml out and back); refresh admin.conf /
           any copied kubeconfigs.


Appendix B: CKA YAML Templates (copy-ready, annotated)
================================================================================

    These templates are copy-ready and annotated: every field carries an inline
    comment explaining WHAT it does and WHY it matters, plus an anatomy callout
    where the structure is non-obvious. They use the easypj project / jobpost app
    convention throughout (Skills, Author, Location, JobPost, auth.User; SQLite in
    dev -> PostgreSQL on Kubernetes). In the exam, paste, then edit names/labels.

    📖 KEY TERM — "anatomy callout": a short note under a template that maps the
       indentation levels to the concepts (spec -> selector -> template -> spec...)
       so you can navigate the YAML by feel, not by counting spaces.

    SECTION MAP
      B.1  Pod (probes, resources, securityContext, volumeMounts)
      B.2  Deployment (strategy maxSurge / maxUnavailable)
      B.3  Services (ClusterIP / NodePort / LoadBalancer / Headless / ExternalName)
      B.4  PersistentVolume + PVC          B.5  StorageClass (dynamic, WaitForFirstConsumer)
      B.6  Role + RoleBinding              B.7  ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding
      B.8  NetworkPolicy (default-deny + allow web->db + allow-DNS egress)
      B.9  ServiceAccount (automount:false) B.10 PodDisruptionBudget
      B.11 Ingress (host/path/TLS)         B.11b Gateway + HTTPRoute (Gateway API)
      B.12 ConfigMap + Secret             B.13 HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA)
      B.14 Job + CronJob                  B.15 StatefulSet (volumeClaimTemplates)
      B.16 LimitRange + ResourceQuota     B.17 CRD + sample CR
      B.18 ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)


    B.1  Pod Template (with all common fields)
         apiVersion: v1                    # Always v1 for pods
         kind: Pod                         # Object type
         metadata:
           name: easypj-web                # Required: unique within namespace
           namespace: easypj               # Omit for default namespace
           labels:                         # Key-value pairs for selection
             app: easypj
             tier: frontend
         spec:
           securityContext:                # Pod-level security (applies to all containers)
             runAsNonRoot: true            # Refuse to start if image runs as root
             runAsUser: 1000               # Numeric UID the process runs as
             fsGroup: 2000                 # Group owner of mounted volumes
           containers:                     # List of containers (at least 1)
           - name: web                     # Container name
             image: easypj:v1              # Image[:tag]
             ports:
             - containerPort: 8000         # Informational, does NOT expose
             env:                          # Environment variables
             - name: DEBUG
               value: "False"
             - name: DB_PASSWORD           # Pull a secret value into env
               valueFrom:
                 secretKeyRef:
                   name: easypj-secret
                   key: DB_PASSWORD
             resources:                    # ALWAYS set in production
               requests:                   # Scheduling guarantee
                 memory: "128Mi"
                 cpu: "250m"
               limits:                     # Hard ceiling
                 memory: "256Mi"
                 cpu: "500m"
             securityContext:              # Container-level (overrides pod-level)
               allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
               readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
               capabilities:
                 drop: ["ALL"]             # Drop all Linux capabilities
             readinessProbe:               # When pod is ready for traffic
               httpGet:
                 path: /health
                 port: 8000
               initialDelaySeconds: 5
             livenessProbe:                # When to restart container
               httpGet:
                 path: /health
                 port: 8000
               initialDelaySeconds: 15
             startupProbe:                 # Protects slow-starting apps from liveness
               httpGet:
                 path: /health
                 port: 8000
               failureThreshold: 30        # 30 x periodSeconds before giving up
               periodSeconds: 10
             volumeMounts:                 # Where volumes appear inside container
             - name: static
               mountPath: /app/static
           volumes:                        # Volumes available to the pod
           - name: static
             emptyDir: {}                  # Ephemeral; gone when pod dies
           restartPolicy: Always           # Always | OnFailure | Never

         ANATOMY: spec.containers[].securityContext beats spec.securityContext on
         conflicts. Probes: startupProbe gates the other two — liveness/readiness
         do not run until startup succeeds. requests drive scheduling; limits drive
         throttling/OOM-kill.

    B.2  Deployment Template (with strategy)
         apiVersion: apps/v1
         kind: Deployment
         metadata:
           name: easypj-web
         spec:
           replicas: 3                     # Desired pod count
           strategy:
             type: RollingUpdate           # RollingUpdate | Recreate
             rollingUpdate:
               maxSurge: 1                 # Extra pods during update
               maxUnavailable: 0           # Zero-downtime update
           selector:
             matchLabels:                  # MUST match template labels (immutable)
               app: easypj
           template:                       # Pod template (same shape as B.1)
             metadata:
               labels:
                 app: easypj
             spec:
               containers:
               - name: web
                 image: easypj:v1

         ANATOMY: selector.matchLabels MUST be a subset of template.metadata.labels
         or the API server rejects the Deployment. maxUnavailable:0 + maxSurge:1 =
         true zero-downtime; Recreate kills all old pods first (brief outage, but
         needed when two versions can't coexist, e.g. an incompatible DB migration).

    B.3  Service Templates (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, Headless, ExternalName)
         # ClusterIP (internal only — default)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: Service
         metadata:
           name: easypj-web
         spec:
           type: ClusterIP                 # Omit type = ClusterIP
           selector:
             app: easypj                   # MUST match pod labels
           ports:
           - port: 80                      # Service port (the VIP listens here)
             targetPort: 8000              # Container port

         # NodePort (external via node IP:port)
         spec:
           type: NodePort
           ports:
           - port: 80
             targetPort: 8000
             nodePort: 30080               # 30000-32767 range

         # LoadBalancer (cloud provider LB)
         spec:
           type: LoadBalancer
           ports:
           - port: 80
             targetPort: 8000

         # Headless (no cluster VIP — DNS returns pod IPs directly; for StatefulSets)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: Service
         metadata:
           name: easypj-db
         spec:
           clusterIP: None                 # THIS makes it headless
           selector:
             app: easypj-db
           ports:
           - port: 5432
             targetPort: 5432

         # ExternalName (CNAME alias to an off-cluster host — no proxying)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: Service
         metadata:
           name: easypj-legacy-db
         spec:
           type: ExternalName
           externalName: db.prod.example.com   # DNS returns this CNAME

         ANATOMY: ClusterIP < NodePort < LoadBalancer is a superset ladder — a
         NodePort Service also gets a ClusterIP; a LoadBalancer also gets a NodePort.
         Headless (clusterIP:None) gives one DNS A record per ready pod, enabling
         stable per-pod names like easypj-db-0.easypj-db.easypj.svc.cluster.local.

    B.4  PersistentVolume + PVC Template
         # PV (admin creates)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: PersistentVolume
         metadata:
           name: easypj-db-pv
         spec:
           capacity:
             storage: 10Gi                 # Storage amount
           accessModes:
           - ReadWriteOnce                 # RWO | ROX | RWX
           persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain  # Retain | Delete | Recycle
           storageClassName: manual        # MUST match PVC
           hostPath:                       # Dev only! Use cloud storage in prod
             path: /data/db

         # PVC (developer creates)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
         metadata:
           name: easypj-db-pvc
         spec:
           accessModes:
           - ReadWriteOnce
           resources:
             requests:
               storage: 10Gi              # Must be <= PV capacity
           storageClassName: manual        # Must match PV

         ANATOMY: binding is a handshake — accessModes + storageClassName + capacity
         must all be compatible. Retain keeps data after the PVC is deleted (PV goes
         to Released, needs manual cleanup); Delete reclaims the backing disk.

    B.5  StorageClass Template (dynamic, WaitForFirstConsumer)
         apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
         kind: StorageClass
         metadata:
           name: fast-storage
         provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner  # Or a cloud provisioner
         volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer     # Delay until pod schedules
         reclaimPolicy: Delete
         allowVolumeExpansion: true                   # Permit PVC grow-in-place

         ANATOMY: WaitForFirstConsumer delays PV creation until a pod using the PVC
         is scheduled, so the volume is provisioned in the SAME zone as the pod —
         avoids the classic "pod pending: volume node affinity conflict" bug.

    B.6  Role + RoleBinding Template
         # Role (namespace-scoped permissions)
         apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
         kind: Role
         metadata:
           namespace: easypj
           name: easypj-role
         rules:
         - apiGroups: [""]                 # "" = core API group
           resources: ["pods", "services"] # What resources
           verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"] # What actions

         # RoleBinding (assigns role to subject)
         apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
         kind: RoleBinding
         metadata:
           namespace: easypj
           name: easypj-binding
         subjects:
         - kind: ServiceAccount
           name: easypj-sa
           namespace: easypj
         roleRef:
           kind: Role
           name: easypj-role
           apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

         ANATOMY: roleRef is immutable — to change the referenced Role you delete and
         recreate the binding. A RoleBinding may reference a ClusterRole (to grant
         cluster-defined permissions but only WITHIN this namespace).

    B.7  ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding Template
         # ClusterRole (cluster-wide permissions — no namespace field)
         apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
         kind: ClusterRole
         metadata:
           name: easypj-cluster-reader
         rules:
         - apiGroups: [""]
           resources: ["nodes", "persistentvolumes"]  # Cluster-scoped resources
           verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]

         # ClusterRoleBinding (grants the ClusterRole cluster-wide)
         apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
         kind: ClusterRoleBinding
         metadata:
           name: easypj-cluster-binding
         subjects:
         - kind: ServiceAccount
           name: easypj-sa
           namespace: easypj
         roleRef:
           kind: ClusterRole
           name: easypj-cluster-reader
           apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

         ANATOMY: same shape as B.6 but cluster-wide and with NO namespace on the
         role objects. Use a ClusterRole + RoleBinding (not ClusterRoleBinding) when
         you want a reusable permission set scoped to one namespace.

    B.8  NetworkPolicy Template (default-deny + allow web->db + allow-DNS egress)
         # 1) Default-deny ALL ingress + egress in the namespace
         apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
         kind: NetworkPolicy
         metadata:
           name: default-deny-all
           namespace: easypj
         spec:
           podSelector: {}                 # Empty = every pod in namespace
           policyTypes:
           - Ingress
           - Egress                        # With no rules below, both are denied

         # 2) Allow web -> db on 5432, plus DNS egress (so name resolution works)
         apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
         kind: NetworkPolicy
         metadata:
           name: db-restrict
           namespace: easypj
         spec:
           podSelector:                    # Apply to these pods (the db)
             matchLabels:
               app: easypj-db
           policyTypes:
           - Ingress
           ingress:
           - from:
             - podSelector:                # Only from the web pods
                 matchLabels:
                   app: easypj-web
             ports:
             - port: 5432                  # Only on this port
         ---
         apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
         kind: NetworkPolicy
         metadata:
           name: allow-dns-egress
           namespace: easypj
         spec:
           podSelector: {}                 # All pods need DNS
           policyTypes:
           - Egress
           egress:
           - to:
             - namespaceSelector: {}       # kube-system CoreDNS
             ports:
             - protocol: UDP
               port: 53
             - protocol: TCP
               port: 53

         ANATOMY: policies are additive and default-allow until the FIRST policy
         selects a pod — then that pod is default-deny for the listed policyTypes.
         GOTCHA: a bare default-deny breaks DNS; always pair it with an allow-DNS
         egress rule or every in-cluster name lookup fails.

    B.9  ServiceAccount Template
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: ServiceAccount
         metadata:
           name: easypj-sa
           namespace: easypj
         automountServiceAccountToken: false  # Security: don't auto-mount the token

         ANATOMY: set automount:false on the SA (or per-pod) so pods that never call
         the API server don't carry a mountable bearer token an attacker could steal.

    B.10 PodDisruptionBudget Template
         apiVersion: policy/v1
         kind: PodDisruptionBudget
         metadata:
           name: easypj-pdb
         spec:
           minAvailable: 2                 # OR maxUnavailable: 1 (pick exactly one)
           selector:
             matchLabels:
               app: easypj

         ANATOMY: a PDB only constrains VOLUNTARY disruptions (kubectl drain, cluster
         autoscaler) — it does NOT protect against node crashes. minAvailable can be
         a percentage ("50%").

    B.11 Ingress Template (host / path / TLS)
         apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
         kind: Ingress
         metadata:
           name: easypj-ingress
           annotations:
             nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
         spec:
           ingressClassName: nginx         # Which Ingress Controller
           tls:                            # Terminate HTTPS at the Ingress
           - hosts:
             - easypj.example.com
             secretName: easypj-tls        # kubernetes.io/tls Secret (crt + key)
           rules:
           - host: easypj.example.com      # Domain name
             http:
               paths:
               - path: /                   # URL path
                 pathType: Prefix
                 backend:
                   service:
                     name: easypj-web      # Target Service
                     port:
                       number: 80

         ANATOMY: the Ingress is inert without a running Ingress Controller that
         claims its ingressClassName. The TLS Secret must be of type kubernetes.io/tls
         and live in the SAME namespace as the Ingress.

    B.11b Gateway + HTTPRoute Template (Gateway API — successor to Ingress)
         apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
         kind: Gateway
         metadata:
           name: easypj-gateway
           namespace: easypj
         spec:
           gatewayClassName: nginx         # Infra: which controller implements it
           listeners:
           - name: http
             protocol: HTTP
             port: 80
             allowedRoutes:
               namespaces:
                 from: Same                # Only routes in this namespace may attach
         ---
         apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
         kind: HTTPRoute
         metadata:
           name: easypj-route
           namespace: easypj
         spec:
           parentRefs:
           - name: easypj-gateway          # Attach to the Gateway above
           hostnames:
           - easypj.example.com
           rules:
           - matches:
             - path:
                 type: PathPrefix
                 value: /
             backendRefs:
             - name: easypj-web            # Target Service
               port: 80

         ANATOMY: Gateway API splits the single Ingress object into role-oriented
         pieces — GatewayClass (provider) / Gateway (infra owner) / HTTPRoute (app
         team) — giving cleaner multi-team delegation than annotation-heavy Ingress.

    B.12 ConfigMap + Secret Template
         # ConfigMap
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: ConfigMap
         metadata:
           name: easypj-config
         data:                             # Key-value pairs (plain text)
           DEBUG: "False"
           DB_HOST: "easypj-db-svc"
           ALLOWED_HOSTS: "*"

         # Secret (values must be base64-encoded)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: Secret
         metadata:
           name: easypj-secret
         type: Opaque
         data:
           SECRET_KEY: c2VjcmV0MTIz        # echo -n 'secret123' | base64
           DB_PASSWORD: cGFzc3dvcmQ=       # echo -n 'password'  | base64

         # (Alternative) stringData lets you skip the base64 step
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: Secret
         metadata:
           name: easypj-secret-plain
         type: Opaque
         stringData:                       # API server base64-encodes for you
           SECRET_KEY: "secret123"

         ANATOMY: data is base64; stringData is plain and auto-encoded on apply.
         GOTCHA: a Secret is only base64 — NOT encrypted at rest unless you enable
         EncryptionConfiguration on etcd.

    B.13 HorizontalPodAutoscaler Template (HPA)
         apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
         kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
         metadata:
           name: easypj-web-hpa
         spec:
           scaleTargetRef:                 # What to scale
             apiVersion: apps/v1
             kind: Deployment
             name: easypj-web
           minReplicas: 2
           maxReplicas: 10
           metrics:
           - type: Resource
             resource:
               name: cpu
               target:
                 type: Utilization
                 averageUtilization: 70    # Scale to keep avg CPU ~70% of requests
           behavior:                       # Optional: tame flapping
             scaleDown:
               stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300

         ANATOMY: HPA needs the metrics-server installed and CPU/memory REQUESTS set
         on the pods (utilization is a % of the request). No requests => HPA can't
         compute a target and stays at minReplicas.

    B.14 Job + CronJob Template
         # Job (run-to-completion, e.g. a one-off Django migration)
         apiVersion: batch/v1
         kind: Job
         metadata:
           name: easypj-migrate
         spec:
           completions: 1                  # How many successful pods needed
           parallelism: 1                  # How many run at once
           backoffLimit: 4                 # Retries before marking Failed
           template:
             spec:
               restartPolicy: OnFailure    # Never | OnFailure (NOT Always)
               containers:
               - name: migrate
                 image: easypj:v1
                 command: ["python", "manage.py", "migrate"]

         # CronJob (scheduled Job — e.g. nightly DB backup)
         apiVersion: batch/v1
         kind: CronJob
         metadata:
           name: easypj-backup
         spec:
           schedule: "0 2 * * *"           # 02:00 daily (cron syntax)
           concurrencyPolicy: Forbid       # Allow | Forbid | Replace
           successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
           jobTemplate:
             spec:
               template:
                 spec:
                   restartPolicy: OnFailure
                   containers:
                   - name: backup
                     image: easypj:v1
                     command: ["sh", "-c", "pg_dump easypj > /backup/db.sql"]

         ANATOMY: a CronJob wraps a Job which wraps a Pod template (three nesting
         levels). restartPolicy MUST be OnFailure or Never — Always is rejected.

    B.15 StatefulSet Template (volumeClaimTemplates)
         apiVersion: apps/v1
         kind: StatefulSet
         metadata:
           name: easypj-db
         spec:
           serviceName: easypj-db          # MUST be a headless Service (see B.3)
           replicas: 3
           selector:
             matchLabels:
               app: easypj-db
           template:
             metadata:
               labels:
                 app: easypj-db
             spec:
               containers:
               - name: postgres
                 image: postgres:16
                 ports:
                 - containerPort: 5432
                 volumeMounts:
                 - name: data
                   mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
           volumeClaimTemplates:           # One PVC PER pod (NOT shared)
           - metadata:
               name: data
             spec:
               accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
               storageClassName: fast-storage
               resources:
                 requests:
                   storage: 10Gi

         ANATOMY: StatefulSet gives STABLE identity — ordinal names (easypj-db-0,
         -1, -2), ordered creation/deletion, and a dedicated PVC per pod via
         volumeClaimTemplates that survives reschedules. Needs the headless Service
         named in serviceName for stable per-pod DNS.

    B.16 LimitRange + ResourceQuota Template
         # LimitRange (per-pod/container defaults & bounds in a namespace)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: LimitRange
         metadata:
           name: easypj-limits
           namespace: easypj
         spec:
           limits:
           - type: Container
             default:                      # Applied if container omits limits
               cpu: "500m"
               memory: "256Mi"
             defaultRequest:               # Applied if container omits requests
               cpu: "250m"
               memory: "128Mi"
             max:
               cpu: "1"
               memory: "512Mi"

         # ResourceQuota (aggregate cap for the whole namespace)
         apiVersion: v1
         kind: ResourceQuota
         metadata:
           name: easypj-quota
           namespace: easypj
         spec:
           hard:
             requests.cpu: "4"
             requests.memory: 8Gi
             limits.cpu: "8"
             limits.memory: 16Gi
             pods: "20"
             persistentvolumeclaims: "5"

         ANATOMY: LimitRange acts per object (defaults + min/max); ResourceQuota caps
         the NAMESPACE total. GOTCHA: once a ResourceQuota on requests/limits exists,
         every new pod MUST specify them — a LimitRange supplies the defaults that
         keep bare pods admissible.

    B.17 CRD + sample Custom Resource Template
         # CustomResourceDefinition (teach the API server a new kind)
         apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
         kind: CustomResourceDefinition
         metadata:
           name: backups.easypj.example.com   # MUST be <plural>.<group>
         spec:
           group: easypj.example.com
           scope: Namespaced               # Namespaced | Cluster
           names:
             plural: backups
             singular: backup
             kind: Backup
             shortNames: ["bk"]
           versions:
           - name: v1
             served: true
             storage: true                 # Exactly one version is the storage one
             schema:
               openAPIV3Schema:
                 type: object
                 properties:
                   spec:
                     type: object
                     properties:
                       schedule: { type: string }
                       retentionDays: { type: integer }

         # Sample Custom Resource (an instance of the new kind)
         apiVersion: easypj.example.com/v1
         kind: Backup
         metadata:
           name: nightly
         spec:
           schedule: "0 2 * * *"
           retentionDays: 7

         ANATOMY: the CRD only adds the TYPE; a controller/operator is what makes a
         Backup object DO anything. The OpenAPI schema gives validation + kubectl
         explain support for your custom kind.

    B.18 ValidatingAdmissionPolicy Template (CEL — built-in policy, no webhook)
         apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
         kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
         metadata:
           name: require-resource-limits
         spec:
           failurePolicy: Fail
           matchConstraints:
             resourceRules:
             - apiGroups: ["apps"]
               apiVersions: ["v1"]
               operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
               resources: ["deployments"]
           validations:
           - expression: >-                # CEL expression — must evaluate true
               object.spec.template.spec.containers.all(c,
                 has(c.resources) && has(c.resources.limits))
             message: "every container must set resources.limits"
         ---
         apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
         kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
         metadata:
           name: require-resource-limits-binding
         spec:
           policyName: require-resource-limits
           validationActions: ["Deny"]     # Deny | Warn | Audit
           matchResources:
             namespaceSelector: {}         # All namespaces

         ANATOMY: this is in-process policy via CEL — no external webhook server to
         run, secure, or scale. The Policy defines the rule; the Binding scopes it to
         namespaces/resources and picks the enforcement action.


    🔑 TEMPLATE QUICK-REFERENCE (which kind for which job)
       ┌──────────────────────────┬───────────────┬─────────────────────────────┐
       │ Need                     │ Kind          │ apiVersion                  │
       ├──────────────────────────┼───────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
       │ One throwaway pod        │ Pod           │ v1                          │
       │ Stateless replicas + roll│ Deployment    │ apps/v1                     │
       │ Stateful, stable IDs+disk│ StatefulSet   │ apps/v1                     │
       │ One pod per node         │ DaemonSet     │ apps/v1                     │
       │ Run-to-completion        │ Job           │ batch/v1                    │
       │ Scheduled job            │ CronJob       │ batch/v1                    │
       │ Stable internal IP       │ Service       │ v1                          │
       │ HTTP routing (L7)        │ Ingress       │ networking.k8s.io/v1        │
       │ HTTP routing (new)       │ Gateway/Route │ gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1│
       │ Durable storage          │ PV / PVC      │ v1                          │
       │ Dynamic storage          │ StorageClass  │ storage.k8s.io/v1           │
       │ Non-secret config        │ ConfigMap     │ v1                          │
       │ Sensitive config         │ Secret        │ v1                          │
       │ NS-scoped permissions    │ Role/RoleBind │ rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1│
       │ Cluster permissions      │ ClusterRole+  │ rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1│
       │ Pod identity to API      │ ServiceAccount│ v1                          │
       │ L3/L4 traffic control    │ NetworkPolicy │ networking.k8s.io/v1        │
       │ Autoscale on metrics     │ HPA           │ autoscaling/v2              │
       │ Protect during drain     │ PDB           │ policy/v1                   │
       │ Per-object limits        │ LimitRange    │ v1                          │
       │ Namespace-wide caps      │ ResourceQuota │ v1                          │
       │ New custom kind          │ CRD           │ apiextensions.k8s.io/v1     │
       │ Built-in CEL policy      │ ValidatingAdm.│ admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1│
       └──────────────────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

    ⚡ SPEED TIP — generate, don't hand-type. Use imperative + dry-run to scaffold,
       then edit:
         kubectl run easypj-web --image=easypj:v1 \
           --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml
         kubectl create deployment easypj-web --image=easypj:v1 \
           --dry-run=client -o yaml > deploy.yaml
         kubectl create service clusterip easypj-web --tcp=80:8000 \
           --dry-run=client -o yaml > svc.yaml
         kubectl create job easypj-migrate --image=easypj:v1 \
           --dry-run=client -o yaml -- python manage.py migrate > job.yaml
       Then add probes/resources/securityContext from B.1 by hand — the generators
       omit those, and the exam rewards adding them.

    🔑 MUST-REMEMBER
       - selector.matchLabels is IMMUTABLE on Deployments/StatefulSets/Jobs.
       - Job/CronJob restartPolicy is OnFailure or Never — never Always.
       - Secret data is base64 (encoding, not encryption); use stringData to skip it.
       - A default-deny NetworkPolicy MUST be paired with an allow-DNS egress rule.
       - HPA needs metrics-server AND resource requests on the pods.
       - StatefulSet needs a headless Service (clusterIP:None) named in serviceName.
       - WaitForFirstConsumer prevents zone-mismatch volume scheduling failures.


Appendix C: Common Errors -> Cause -> Fix
================================================================================

  This appendix is your fast triage table. ~90% of Kubernetes incidents are
  diagnosed by the same two-step reflex: describe (READ THE EVENTS) + logs
  --previous. Then isolate by layer: pod -> node/kubelet -> control plane
  (crictl) -> network/DNS. The first table below is the compact lookup card
  (Edition-1 style). The second is the expanded triage matrix that adds the
  FIRST COMMAND to run for each symptom. Use the compact card for memory recall
  under exam pressure; use the expanded matrix when you actually need to act.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  C.1  Quick reference card — error -> cause -> fix
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    | Error                           | Cause                         | Fix                        |
    | CrashLoopBackOff                | App crash / missing config    | Check logs, fix config     |
    | ImagePullBackOff                | Wrong image / no registry auth| Fix image or add secret    |
    | Pending (pod)                   | No resources / no matching PV | Add resources or create PV |
    | Pending (PVC)                   | No matching PV or SC          | Create PV or fix SC        |
    | NodeNotReady                    | kubelet down / resource issue | SSH, check kubelet, restart|
    | FailedScheduling                | Taints / affinity mismatch    | Check taints, tolerations  |
    | Forbidden                       | RBAC insufficient permissions | Add Role/ClusterRole       |
    | connection refused              | Service/pod not running       | Check target pod status    |
    | certificate has expired         | Cert past validity period     | kubeadm certs renew        |
    | etcd cluster is unavailable     | etcd down / cert issue        | Check etcd pods/certs      |
    | unable to connect to server     | kubeconfig wrong / API down   | Fix kubeconfig / check API |

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  C.2  Expanded triage matrix — symptom -> first command -> cause -> fix
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┬────────────┐
  │ SYMPTOM              │ FIRST COMMAND     │ LIKELY CAUSE      │ FIX         │
  ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────┼────────────┤
  │ CrashLoopBackOff     │ logs --previous  │ app crash / bad   │ fix config/ │
  │                      │ + describe       │ config / OOM      │ probe/dep   │
  │ ImagePullBackOff /   │ describe (Events)│ wrong image:tag / │ fix image;  │
  │ ErrImagePull         │                  │ no pull secret    │ add regcred │
  │ CreateContainer-     │ describe         │ missing ConfigMap │ create the  │
  │ ConfigError          │                  │ /Secret/key       │ CM/Secret   │
  │ Pod Pending          │ describe (Events)│ no res / taint /  │ free res /  │
  │                      │                  │ affinity / no node│ tolerate    │
  │ PVC Pending          │ describe pvc     │ no matching PV /  │ create PV / │
  │                      │                  │ wrong SC / no     │ fix class / │
  │                      │                  │ provisioner       │ install CSI │
  │ OOMKilled (137)      │ describe (Last   │ mem limit too low │ raise limit/│
  │                      │ State)           │ / leak            │ fix leak    │
  │ Node NotReady        │ ssh; systemctl   │ kubelet down /CNI │ start kubelet│
  │                      │ status kubelet;  │ missing / swap on │ /install CNI│
  │                      │ journalctl -u    │ / disk pressure   │ /swapoff /  │
  │                      │ kubelet          │                   │ free disk   │
  │ FailedScheduling     │ describe (Events)│ taint/affinity/   │ tolerate /  │
  │                      │                  │ insufficient req  │ fix rules   │
  │ Forbidden (RBAC)     │ auth can-i .. --as│ missing Role/    │ create Role+│
  │                      │                  │ Binding           │ Binding     │
  │ Service: no endpoints│ get endpoints    │ selector!=labels /│ fix selector│
  │                      │                  │ no ready pods     │ /readiness  │
  │ connection refused   │ get ep; exec curl│ pod down / wrong  │ fix pod /   │
  │                      │ from temp pod    │ targetPort/NetPol │ port/policy │
  │ DNS NXDOMAIN         │ exec nslookup    │ CoreDNS down /    │ fix Corefile│
  │                      │ from temp pod    │ wrong FQDN/ndots  │ / use FQDN  │
  │ certificate expired  │ kubeadm certs    │ leaf cert > 1y    │ certs renew │
  │                      │ check-expiration │                   │ all;restart │
  │ etcd unavailable     │ crictl ps/logs;  │ etcd down / cert /│ fix manifest│
  │                      │ etcdctl endpoint │ quorum lost       │ /restore    │
  │                      │ health           │                   │             │
  │ apiserver refused    │ crictl ps -a;    │ bad apiserver     │ fix manifest│
  │ (kubectl is dead)    │ crictl logs;     │ static-pod        │ — kubelet   │
  │                      │ journalctl -u    │ manifest          │ auto-restarts│
  │                      │ kubelet          │                   │             │
  │ Ingress not routing  │ get ingress; get │ no controller /   │ install /   │
  │                      │ pods -n ingress  │ wrong class       │ set class   │
  └──────────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────┴────────────┘
  💡 ~90% start with: describe (READ THE EVENTS) + logs --previous. Then isolate
     by layer: pod -> node/kubelet -> control plane (crictl) -> network/DNS.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  C.3  Copy-paste triage templates
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  🧪 The universal first move (works for almost any failing pod):

      kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> | sed -n '/Events/,$p'
      kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous       # last crashed container
      kubectl get events -n <ns> --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail

  🧪 CrashLoopBackOff drill-down:

      kubectl logs <pod> -n <ns> --previous
      kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>          # Last State + Exit Code
      # Exit 1=app error  137=OOMKilled/SIGKILL  143=SIGTERM  0=clean exit

  🧪 ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull (easypj app image):

      kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>          # read Events for the reason
      # private registry -> create + reference an imagePullSecret:
      kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred \
        --docker-server=<registry> --docker-username=<u> \
        --docker-password=<p> -n <ns>
      # then add to pod/deploy spec: imagePullSecrets: [{name: regcred}]

  🧪 Pod / PVC Pending:

      kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>          # FailedScheduling reason
      kubectl get pv,pvc,sc -n <ns>               # PVC: matching PV/SC?
      kubectl describe pvc <pvc> -n <ns>          # provisioner / class issue

  🧪 Service has no endpoints (easypj reachable internally?):

      kubectl get endpoints <svc> -n <ns>         # empty => selector mismatch
      kubectl get pods -n <ns> --show-labels      # compare to svc selector
      kubectl run tmp --image=busybox:1.36 -it --rm --restart=Never -n <ns> \
        -- wget -qO- http://<svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:<port>

  🧪 DNS resolution check:

      kubectl run tmp --image=busybox:1.36 -it --rm --restart=Never -- \
        nslookup <svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local
      kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns   # CoreDNS up?
      kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns

  🧪 Control plane down (kubectl itself fails) — go node-local:

      sudo crictl ps -a                           # are static pods running?
      sudo crictl logs <container-id>             # apiserver/etcd logs
      sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f               # kubelet must be running
      ls /etc/kubernetes/manifests/               # fix the static-pod YAML

  🧪 Certificate expiry / renewal:

      sudo kubeadm certs check-expiration
      sudo kubeadm certs renew all
      # then restart control-plane static pods (move-out/move-in the manifests
      # or: sudo crictl rm <apiserver/controller/scheduler containers>)

  🧪 Node NotReady:

      kubectl describe node <node>                # Conditions + taints
      ssh <node>; systemctl status kubelet
      journalctl -u kubelet | tail -50
      swapoff -a                                  # swap must be OFF
      # check CNI plugin pods on that node; check disk/PID/mem pressure

  🧪 RBAC Forbidden:

      kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> -n <ns> \
        --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>
      # create the missing Role + RoleBinding (or ClusterRole/Binding)
      kubectl create role <name> --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods -n <ns>
      kubectl create rolebinding <name> --role=<name> \
        --serviceaccount=<ns>:<sa> -n <ns>

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  C.4  Exit-code & condition glossary
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    | Signal / Code     | Meaning                                            |
    | Exit 0            | Container exited cleanly (may still loop if job)   |
    | Exit 1            | Generic app error — read the logs                  |
    | Exit 137 (128+9)  | SIGKILL — usually OOMKilled (mem limit) or evicted |
    | Exit 143 (128+15) | SIGTERM — graceful shutdown / liveness restart     |
    | CrashLoopBackOff  | Container keeps crashing; kubelet backs off restart|
    | ImagePullBackOff  | Cannot pull image; backing off pull retries        |
    | ErrImagePull      | First pull attempt failed (auth / tag / network)   |
    | CreateContainer-  | Referenced ConfigMap/Secret/key/volume missing     |
    |   ConfigError     |                                                    |
    | OOMKilled         | Memory limit exceeded; kernel killed the container |
    | Evicted           | Node resource pressure (disk/mem) evicted the pod  |
    | Pending           | Not yet scheduled — no fit (res/taint/affinity/PV) |
    | NodeNotReady      | kubelet not reporting healthy on that node         |
    | Forbidden (403)   | RBAC denies the request — add Role/ClusterRole     |
    | Unauthorized (401)| Bad/expired credentials or token                   |

  🔑 MUST-REMEMBER: The Events section of `kubectl describe` and a
     `kubectl logs --previous` resolve the overwhelming majority of pod
     failures. When kubectl itself is unreachable, the control plane is down —
     drop to the node and use crictl + journalctl -u kubelet, then repair the
     static-pod manifests in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/.


================================================================================
  Appendix D: Kubernetes Glossary (120+ terms, A->Z)
================================================================================

    The definitive merged term list — every entry from both editions, folded
    together A->Z and de-duplicated. CKA-relevant definitions throughout.

    Legend:  [C] = cluster-scoped   [N] = namespaced   🎯 = exam-critical

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── A ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Admission Controller 🎯 — intercepts API requests AFTER authN/authZ and
       BEFORE persistence to etcd; mutating controllers run first, then
       validating controllers.
    Affinity 🎯 — rules biasing pod placement (node/pod, required/preferred);
       expresses placement preferences and attractions.
    Aggregation Layer — extends the apiserver via APIService objects so extra
       APIs appear under the same front door.
    Annotation — non-identifying key/value metadata; NOT used for selection
       (contrast with Label, which IS selectable).
    API Group 🎯 — logical grouping of API resources: core "", apps, batch,
       networking.k8s.io, storage.k8s.io, rbac.authorization.k8s.io, ...
    API Server (kube-apiserver) 🎯 — the central management hub and ONLY front
       door; every request flows authN -> authZ -> admission -> etcd.
    AppArmor — kernel LSM (Linux Security Module) restricting a container's
       file/network access.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── B ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Base64 🎯 — ENCODING, not encryption — the form Secret values are stored in
       (always pair with encryption-at-rest).
    BGP — Border Gateway Protocol; routing protocol some CNIs (Calico) use for
       pod networking.
    BoltDB — the embedded on-disk store etcd uses (paired with a WAL).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── C ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    cAdvisor — per-node container resource metrics, embedded in the kubelet.
    Calico — CNI plugin WITH NetworkPolicy support (BGP or VXLAN backend).
    Capability (Linux) — granular slice of root privilege; drop ALL to harden.
    CertificateSigningRequest (CSR) 🎯 — request a certificate signed by the
       cluster CA.
    cgroup — Linux kernel feature limiting CPU/memory per process group.
    CIDR 🎯 — Classless Inter-Domain Routing; IP-range notation
       (e.g. --pod-network-cidr=10.244.0.0/16).
    Cilium — eBPF-based CNI (networking, NetworkPolicy, Hubble observability).
    ClusterIP 🎯 — default Service type; internal-only virtual IP.
    ClusterRole [C] 🎯 — cluster-wide permission set.
    CNI 🎯 — Container Network Interface; the plugin plug-point for pod
       networking.
    ConfigMap [N] 🎯 — non-sensitive key/value configuration data.
    Container Runtime — software that actually runs containers
       (containerd, CRI-O).
    containerd — industry-standard default container runtime (implements CRI).
    Context (kubeconfig) 🎯 — a cluster + user + namespace tuple selected in
       ~/.kube/config.
    Control Plane 🎯 — the brain of the cluster: apiserver + etcd + scheduler +
       controller-manager.
    Controller — reconciliation loop driving actual state -> desired state.
    CoreDNS 🎯 — the in-cluster DNS server (a Deployment in kube-system).
    Cordon 🎯 — mark a node unschedulable (existing pods stay put).
    CRI 🎯 — Container Runtime Interface; the runtime plug-point.
    CronJob [N] 🎯 — runs Jobs on a cron schedule (like Linux cron).
    CSI 🎯 — Container Storage Interface; the storage plug-point.
    CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) [C] 🎯 — extends the Kubernetes API with a
       new custom resource type.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── D ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    DaemonSet [N] 🎯 — ensures exactly one pod per matching node.
    Defragmentation — reclaim etcd disk space after compaction.
    Deployment [N] 🎯 — manages ReplicaSets for declarative, rolling updates of
       stateless apps.
    Descheduler — evicts pods to re-balance against current policy (add-on).
    Drain 🎯 — safely evict all pods from a node for maintenance.
    Dynamic Provisioning 🎯 — a StorageClass auto-creates a PV to satisfy a PVC.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── E ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    eBPF — extended Berkeley Packet Filter; kernel tech powering modern
       CNIs/observability (Cilium).
    emptyDir 🎯 — ephemeral pod-scoped volume created when the pod starts and
       deleted when the pod ends (scratch/sidecar).
    Endpoint / EndpointSlice 🎯 — the pod IP:Port combinations backing a
       Service.
    etcd 🎯 — distributed key-value store holding ALL cluster state (Raft
       consensus).
    Eviction — removing a pod due to node resource pressure or a drain.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── F ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Finalizer — blocks object deletion until cleanup completes.
    Flannel — simple VXLAN overlay CNI (NO NetworkPolicy support).
    FQDN 🎯 — fully-qualified name: <svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local.
    fsGroup — supplemental GID applied to mounted volumes.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── G ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Gateway API 🎯 — role-based successor to Ingress
       (GatewayClass / Gateway / HTTPRoute).
    GitOps — git as the source of truth; a controller syncs (ArgoCD / Flux).
    Guaranteed (QoS) 🎯 — requests == limits for all resources (highest QoS).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── H ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    HA 🎯 — High Availability: >=3 control planes + quorum etcd + load balancer.
    Headless Service 🎯 — clusterIP: None; per-pod DNS records (StatefulSets).
    Helm 🎯 — Kubernetes package manager; templated, versioned releases
       (charts).
    hostPath 🎯 — volume mounting the node's filesystem into the pod
       (dev/agent only!).
    HPA [N] 🎯 — Horizontal Pod Autoscaler; scales replicas based on metrics.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── I ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Informer — client-side cache/watch primitive powering controllers.
    Ingress [N] 🎯 — L7 HTTP/HTTPS routing rules for Services (needs a
       controller).
    Ingress Controller 🎯 — the component that implements Ingress rules
       (nginx, traefik).
    initContainer 🎯 — runs to completion BEFORE the app containers start
       (setup tasks).
    IPVS — high-performance kube-proxy mode (kernel hash tables vs iptables).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── J ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Job [N] 🎯 — run-to-completion workload.
    JSONPath 🎯 — query language for JSON, used with kubectl -o jsonpath.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── K ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    kubeadm 🎯 — tool to bootstrap & upgrade Kubernetes clusters.
    kubeconfig 🎯 — clusters/users/contexts file (~/.kube/config).
    kubectl 🎯 — the CLI / REST client for interacting with Kubernetes.
    kubelet 🎯 — node agent that runs pods (a systemd service, NOT a pod).
    kube-proxy 🎯 — network proxy programming Service routing per node
       (iptables / IPVS / nftables).
    kube-scheduler 🎯 — places pods on nodes: filter -> score -> bind.
    Kustomize 🎯 — template-free, Kubernetes-native config: base + overlays /
       patches (kubectl apply -k).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── L ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Label 🎯 — key/value pair attached to objects, used for selection.
    Lease — lightweight resource for leader election and node heartbeats.
    LimitRange [N] 🎯 — set default/min/max resource limits per
       pod/container in a namespace.
    Liveness Probe 🎯 — check if the container is alive; restart it if failing.
    LoadBalancer 🎯 — Service type provisioning an external load balancer.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── M ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Manifest — YAML/JSON file declaring the desired state of K8s objects.
    Metrics Server 🎯 — supplies kubectl top metrics and HPA inputs.
    Mirror Pod — the read-only API representation of a static pod.
    Mutating Webhook — admission webhook that can modify a request in flight.
    MVCC — etcd multi-version concurrency control (revisions).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── N ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Namespace [C] 🎯 — a virtual cluster within a cluster for isolation.
    NetworkPolicy [N] 🎯 — firewall rules for pod network traffic (needs a
       policy-aware CNI).
    Node [C] 🎯 — a worker or control-plane machine in the cluster.
    NodePort 🎯 — Service type exposing on each node's IP:port (30000-32767).
    nodeSelector / Node Affinity 🎯 — constrain pods to specific nodes.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── O ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    OCI — Open Container Initiative; container image/runtime standard.
    OOMKilled 🎯 — container killed for exceeding its memory limit.
    OPA Gatekeeper — Rego-based policy engine implemented as a webhook.
    Operator 🎯 — custom controller + CRD automating a complex app's lifecycle.
    ownerReferences — parent links enabling cascading deletion.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── P ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    PersistentVolume (PV) [C] 🎯 — cluster-level storage resource.
    PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) [N] 🎯 — a user's request for persistent
       storage.
    PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) [N] 🎯 — min available pods during voluntary
       disruption.
    Pod [N] 🎯 — smallest deployable unit; one or more containers sharing
       network/storage.
    Pod Security Standards / Admission 🎯 — three profiles enforced per
       namespace: Privileged, Baseline, Restricted.
    PriorityClass [C] — pod importance for scheduling and preemption.
    Probe 🎯 — health check (Liveness / Readiness / Startup).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── Q ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    QoS Class 🎯 — Guaranteed / Burstable / BestEffort (determines eviction
       order under pressure).
    Quorum 🎯 — N/2+1 etcd members required to commit a write.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── R ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Raft 🎯 — etcd's consensus protocol (leader + followers).
    RBAC 🎯 — Role-Based Access Control.
    Readiness Probe 🎯 — check if the pod is ready for traffic; add/remove from
       Service endpoints accordingly.
    Reclaim Policy 🎯 — what happens to a PV when its PVC is deleted:
       Retain / Delete / Recycle.
    ReplicaSet [N] 🎯 — ensures the desired number of pod replicas (managed by
       Deployments).
    ResourceQuota [N] 🎯 — limit total resource consumption per namespace.
    Role [N] 🎯 — namespaced permission set.
    RoleBinding [N] 🎯 — binds a Role to a subject (user/group/SA) within a
       namespace.
    Rolling Update 🎯 — deploy a new version gradually, replacing old pods one
       by one (default strategy).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── S ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Secret [N] 🎯 — stores sensitive data, base64-encoded (encrypt at rest!).
    SecurityContext 🎯 — security settings for a pod/container.
    seccomp — syscall filtering (RuntimeDefault recommended).
    Selector 🎯 — match labels to identify a set of objects.
    Service [N] 🎯 — stable VIP + DNS endpoint fronting a set of pods.
    ServiceAccount [N] 🎯 — identity pods use to authenticate to the API.
    Sidecar — additional helper container in a pod (logging, proxy, etc.).
    StatefulSet [N] 🎯 — manages stateful apps with stable identity +
       per-pod storage.
    Static Pod 🎯 — pod managed directly by the kubelet from
       /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ (not via the API server).
    StorageClass [C] 🎯 — defines a type of storage for dynamic provisioning.
    Startup Probe 🎯 — protects slow-starting containers from premature
       liveness restarts.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── T ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Taint / Toleration 🎯 — a Taint marks a node to repel pods; a Toleration
       lets a pod schedule on the tainted node anyway.
    TLS 🎯 — mutual TLS secures all control-plane traffic.
    TokenRequest — issues short-lived, projected ServiceAccount tokens.
    Topology Spread Constraint 🎯 — even pod distribution across failure
       domains.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── U ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Uncordon 🎯 — make a cordoned node schedulable again.
    Union FS (OverlayFS) — the layered container filesystem.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── V ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 🎯 — in-cluster CEL policy (no webhook needed).
    Validating Webhook — admission webhook that accepts/rejects a request.
    Velero — backup/restore of namespaces plus PV snapshots.
    veth pair — virtual ethernet linking a pod to the node bridge.
    Volume — storage attached to a pod.
    volumeClaimTemplates 🎯 — per-pod PVCs in a StatefulSet.
    volumeMode — Filesystem (default) or Block.
    VolumeMount — how a volume is mounted inside a container.
    VPA — Vertical Pod Autoscaler (right-sizes resource requests).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ── W ──
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    WaitForFirstConsumer 🎯 — delay PV binding until a consuming pod schedules.
    WAL — etcd write-ahead log.
    Webhook — HTTP callback used by admission control.
    Worker Node 🎯 — node that runs application pods.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  📖 HOW TO USE THIS GLOSSARY IN THE EXAM
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    • Any term tagged 🎯 is fair game on the CKA — drill these first.
    • [C] vs [N] tells you the scope: cluster-scoped objects ignore -n, while
      namespaced objects must be created/queried in the right namespace.
    • When stuck on a resource name, run:  kubectl api-resources | grep <hint>
      to confirm its API group, scope (NAMESPACED column) and short name.
    • Cross-reference: a 📖 key term here usually maps to a full chapter section
      earlier in this guide — use the SECTION MAP to jump back.

    E.1   Namespace
    E.2   ConfigMap
    E.3   Secret

    E.7   Ingress
    E.7b  Gateway API: Gateway + HTTPRoute (modern alternative to Ingress)
    E.8   NetworkPolicy
    E.9   RBAC (ServiceAccount + Role + RoleBinding)
    E.10  PodDisruptionBudget

    E.13  Dockerfile (multi-stage) + .dockerignore
