  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  J.1  THE THREE-TIER RESOURCE MODEL (who owns what)        🎯 🟢
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    The whole point is SEPARATION OF CONCERNS. Three roles, three resource
    layers, three owners — and each layer references the one above it.

      ROLE                  RESOURCE          OWNS / DECIDES
      ┌───────────────────┬─────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
      │ Infrastructure    │ GatewayClass    │ which controller / LB         │
      │ provider          │ (cluster-scoped)│ implementation backs Gateways │
      ├───────────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
      │ Cluster operator  │ Gateway         │ listeners: ports, protocol,   │
      │ (platform team)   │ (namespaced)    │ TLS certs, allowedRoutes      │
      ├───────────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
      │ Application dev   │ HTTPRoute /     │ hostnames, paths, headers,    │
      │ (jobpost team)    │ GRPCRoute/...   │ which Services get traffic    │
      └───────────────────┴─────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘

    How the layers bind together (top references downward, routes point UP):

      GatewayClass  "cloud-lb"   ◀── installed by infra/controller vendor
            ▲  gatewayClassName
            │
      ┌─────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ Gateway  easypj-gw   (ns: infra)                     │
      │   listeners:                                         │
      │     - name: https   port: 443  protocol: HTTPS  TLS  │
      │     - name: http    port: 80   protocol: HTTP        │
      │   allowedRoutes: {namespaces: {from: Selector ...}}  │
      └─────▲───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
            │ parentRefs  (route attaches to Gateway+listener)
      ┌─────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ HTTPRoute  jobpost-route  (ns: jobpost)              │
      │   hostnames: ["easypj.example.com"]                  │
      │   rules:                                             │
      │     - matches: [path: /jobs]                         │
      │       backendRefs: [Service jobpost-svc:8000]        │
      └─────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                │ backendRef
                                ▼
                       Service jobpost-svc ──▶ Pods (easypj/jobpost)

    🧠 ANALOGY: GatewayClass is the MAKE of a car (who built it), the Gateway
    is YOUR car parked in the driveway (the doors/ports you opened), and an
    HTTPRoute is a passenger's destination card ("take me to /jobs").

    💡 INSIGHT: Routes live in the APPLICATION namespace but attach to a
    Gateway possibly in ANOTHER namespace. This is the feature Ingress never
    had: the platform team owns one Gateway + TLS cert, and many app teams
    bring their own routes without touching it.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  J.2  RESOURCE REFERENCE                                   🎯 🟡
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    API group: gateway.networking.k8s.io   (CRDs — must be installed first)

    ┌──────────────┬───────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
    │ Kind         │ Scope     │ Stable group │ Purpose                       │
    ├──────────────┼───────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
    │ GatewayClass │ Cluster   │ v1           │ template/impl for Gateways    │
    │ Gateway      │ Namespaced│ v1           │ listeners (ports/TLS), addrs  │
    │ HTTPRoute    │ Namespaced│ v1           │ L7 HTTP routing rules         │
    │ GRPCRoute    │ Namespaced│ v1           │ L7 gRPC routing (method match)│
    │ TLSRoute     │ Namespaced│ v1alpha2     │ SNI-based TLS passthrough     │
    │ TCPRoute     │ Namespaced│ v1alpha2     │ raw L4 TCP forwarding         │
    │ UDPRoute     │ Namespaced│ v1alpha2     │ raw L4 UDP forwarding         │
    │ ReferenceGrant│Namespaced│ v1beta1      │ allow cross-ns references     │
    └──────────────┴───────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
    ⚠️ Only GatewayClass/Gateway/HTTPRoute (+GRPCRoute) are v1 GA. The L4
       routes (TLS/TCP/UDP) remain experimental (v1alpha2) in 2025.

    --- GatewayClass (infra provider) ---
      apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
      kind: GatewayClass
      metadata:
        name: cloud-lb
      spec:
        controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller   # picks the impl

    --- Gateway (cluster operator) ---
      apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
      kind: Gateway
      metadata:
        name: easypj-gw
        namespace: infra
      spec:
        gatewayClassName: cloud-lb
        listeners:
          - name: https
            protocol: HTTPS
            port: 443
            tls:
              mode: Terminate
              certificateRefs:
                - kind: Secret
                  name: easypj-tls          # TLS cert/key Secret
            allowedRoutes:
              namespaces:
                from: Selector              # All | Same | Selector
                selector:
                  matchLabels:
                    gateway-access: "true"  # only ns with this label

    --- HTTPRoute (application developer) ---
      apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
      kind: HTTPRoute
      metadata:
        name: jobpost-route
        namespace: jobpost
      spec:
        parentRefs:
          - name: easypj-gw
            namespace: infra
            sectionName: https              # attach to the 'https' listener
        hostnames:
          - "easypj.example.com"
        rules:
          - matches:
              - path:
                  type: PathPrefix
                  value: /jobs
            backendRefs:
              - name: jobpost-svc
                port: 8000

    🔧 PathPrefix vs Exact vs RegularExpression: type: PathPrefix is the
    common one; Exact must match the whole path; RegularExpression support is
    implementation-specific (not guaranteed portable).

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  J.3  STATUS CONDITIONS CHEAT-SHEET (how to debug)         🎯 🩺 🟡
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Everything in Gateway API reports health through .status[].conditions.
    Debugging = `kubectl describe` the resource and read the conditions.

    GATEWAY conditions (.status.conditions):
    ┌──────────────┬────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ Type         │ Good   │ Means / when False look at...                 │
    ├──────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Accepted     │ True   │ controller accepted the Gateway spec          │
    │ Programmed   │ True   │ underlying LB/dataplane actually configured;  │
    │              │        │ .status.addresses gets the real IP/host       │
    └──────────────┴────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    GATEWAY LISTENER conditions (.status.listeners[].conditions):
    ┌────────────────┬──────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ Type           │ Good │ Means / when False look at...                   │
    ├────────────────┼──────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Accepted       │ True │ listener config valid                           │
    │ Programmed     │ True │ listener live on the dataplane                  │
    │ ResolvedRefs   │ True │ TLS certificateRefs / backends resolved OK      │
    │ Conflicted     │ False│ no two listeners clash on port/hostname         │
    └────────────────┴──────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    (.status.listeners[].attachedRoutes = how many routes bound — sanity check)

    HTTPROUTE conditions (.status.parents[].conditions):
    ┌────────────────┬──────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ Type           │ Good │ Means / when False look at...                   │
    ├────────────────┼──────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Accepted       │ True │ Gateway accepted the attachment                 │
    │ ResolvedRefs   │ True │ all backendRefs (Services) exist & port valid   │
    └────────────────┴──────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    🩺 Common reason strings to recognise:
      NotAllowedByListeners  -> Route namespace blocked by allowedRoutes
      NoMatchingListenerHostname -> route hostname not covered by listener
      RefNotPermitted        -> cross-ns backendRef without a ReferenceGrant
      BackendNotFound        -> Service name/port wrong
      InvalidCertificateRef  -> TLS Secret missing/wrong kind

      ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ DEBUG FLOW:  describe HTTPRoute  →  Accepted? ResolvedRefs?        │
      │   if NotAllowedByListeners → fix Gateway allowedRoutes / ns label  │
      │   if BackendNotFound       → fix backendRefs name/port             │
      │   else describe Gateway    → Programmed? listener ResolvedRefs?    │
      │   no address on Gateway    → controller not running / no LB        │
      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  J.4  GATEWAY API vs INGRESS (side-by-side)               🎯 🧭 🟢
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ┌────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
    │ Concern            │ Ingress               │ Gateway API             │
    ├────────────────────┼───────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┤
    │ API status         │ frozen (net/v1)       │ active, GA v1 (CRDs)    │
    │ Roles              │ one object, mixed     │ 3 roles, 3 resources    │
    │ Portability        │ vendor annotations    │ portable spec fields    │
    │ Protocols          │ HTTP/HTTPS only       │ HTTP/gRPC/TLS/TCP/UDP   │
    │ Header routing     │ annotation-only       │ first-class match field │
    │ Traffic splitting  │ annotation-only       │ backendRef weights      │
    │ TLS                │ spec.tls (terminate)  │ Terminate or Passthrough│
    │ Cross-namespace    │ no                    │ yes (+ReferenceGrant)   │
    │ Redirect/rewrite   │ annotation-only       │ standard filters        │
    │ East-west / mesh   │ no                    │ yes (GAMMA)             │
    │ Built into k8s?    │ yes (core API)        │ no (install CRDs)       │
    └────────────────────┴───────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘

    🧭 DECISION GUIDE
      - Brand-new platform, want portability/headers/splitting → Gateway API.
      - Simple host/path only, existing nginx-ingress, no churn → Ingress is
        fine (still supported, just frozen).
      - Need gRPC routing, TLS passthrough, or mesh east-west → Gateway API
        (Ingress cannot express these).

    Mental translation Ingress -> HTTPRoute:
      Ingress rule host         -> HTTPRoute.spec.hostnames
      Ingress path + pathType   -> rules[].matches[].path (PathPrefix/Exact)
      Ingress backend service   -> rules[].backendRefs (name+port)
      ingressClassName          -> Gateway.spec.gatewayClassName (one level up)
      spec.tls + Secret         -> Gateway listener tls.certificateRefs

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  J.5  COMMON PATTERNS (templates)                         🎯 🧪 🟡
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    --- PATH ROUTING (fan one host to two Services) ---
      rules:
        - matches: [{ path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /jobs } }]
          backendRefs: [{ name: jobpost-svc, port: 8000 }]
        - matches: [{ path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /admin } }]
          backendRefs: [{ name: easypj-admin-svc, port: 8000 }]

    --- HEADER ROUTING (canary by header) ---
      rules:
        - matches:
            - headers:
                - name: x-canary
                  type: Exact
                  value: "true"
          backendRefs: [{ name: jobpost-canary, port: 8000 }]
        - matches: [{ path: { type: PathPrefix, value: / } }]
          backendRefs: [{ name: jobpost-svc, port: 8000 }]

    --- WEIGHTED TRAFFIC SPLIT (90/10 canary) ---
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - name: jobpost-svc      # stable
              port: 8000
              weight: 90
            - name: jobpost-canary   # new version
              port: 8000
              weight: 10
      ⚡ Weights are RELATIVE, not percentages — 9:1 == 90:10. weight 0 drains.

    --- HTTPS / TLS TERMINATION (on the Gateway listener) ---
      # Gateway side:
      listeners:
        - name: https
          protocol: HTTPS
          port: 443
          tls:
            mode: Terminate
            certificateRefs:
              - kind: Secret
                name: easypj-tls
      # mode: Passthrough  -> use a TLSRoute (SNI), no cert on the Gateway

    --- HTTP -> HTTPS REDIRECT (filter, no backend) ---
      rules:
        - filters:
            - type: RequestRedirect
              requestRedirect:
                scheme: https
                statusCode: 301

    --- URL REWRITE (strip /jobs prefix) ---
      rules:
        - matches: [{ path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /jobs } }]
          filters:
            - type: URLRewrite
              urlRewrite:
                path:
                  type: ReplacePrefixMatch
                  replacePrefixMatch: /
          backendRefs: [{ name: jobpost-svc, port: 8000 }]

    --- REQUEST HEADER MODIFIER (add/set/remove) ---
      filters:
        - type: RequestHeaderModifier
          requestHeaderModifier:
            add:    [{ name: x-env, value: prod }]
            set:    [{ name: x-app, value: easypj }]
            remove: [ x-internal-debug ]

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  J.6  CROSS-NAMESPACE ROUTING & ReferenceGrant            🎯 🔧 🔴
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Two independent cross-namespace gates — BOTH must say yes:

      (1) Route -> Gateway: controlled by the Gateway's listener
          allowedRoutes.namespaces (from: All | Same | Selector). The
          GATEWAY owner decides which route namespaces may attach.

      (2) Route -> backend in another namespace, OR Gateway TLS Secret in
          another namespace: controlled by a ReferenceGrant in the TARGET
          namespace. The OWNER of the referenced object must opt in.

      ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ ns: jobpost                         ns: payments                  │
      │  HTTPRoute  ──backendRef──▶  (Service billing-svc)                 │
      │                                   ▲                               │
      │                                   │ permitted by                  │
      │                            ReferenceGrant (in ns payments)        │
      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

      apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
      kind: ReferenceGrant
      metadata:
        name: allow-jobpost-to-billing
        namespace: payments              # lives WITH the target
      spec:
        from:
          - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
            kind: HTTPRoute
            namespace: jobpost           # who may reference
        to:
          - group: ""
            kind: Service                # what may be referenced
            name: billing-svc            # optional: restrict to one

    ⚠️ Without a ReferenceGrant a cross-ns backendRef fails with
       RefNotPermitted in the HTTPRoute's ResolvedRefs condition — the route
       is "Accepted" but sends no traffic. This is the #1 cross-ns gotcha.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  J.7  kubectl COMMANDS & GLOSSARY                          🎯 ⚡
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    kubectl get gatewayclass
    kubectl get gateway -A
    kubectl get httproute -A
    kubectl describe gateway easypj-gw -n infra        # read conditions
    kubectl describe httproute jobpost-route -n jobpost
    kubectl get gateway easypj-gw -n infra \
      -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[0].value}'       # the public IP/host
    kubectl get gateway -A \
      -o custom-columns=NS:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,\
CLASS:.spec.gatewayClassName,PROGRAMMED:'.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Programmed")].status'
    kubectl api-resources --api-group=gateway.networking.k8s.io
    kubectl explain httproute.spec.rules.backendRefs

    Short names: gateway -> gtw (impl-dependent), httproute (no short name).

    GLOSSARY
      parentRefs ...... on a Route; which Gateway(s)/listener it attaches to.
      sectionName ..... on parentRefs; the specific listener name to bind to.
      backendRefs ..... on a Route rule; target Service(s) (+port,+weight).
      listeners ....... on a Gateway; port+protocol+TLS+allowedRoutes entries.
      allowedRoutes ... on a listener; which route namespaces may attach.
      certificateRefs . on a listener tls; Secret(s) holding the TLS cert/key.
      filters ......... per-rule transforms: redirect, rewrite, header mod.
      weight .......... relative share of traffic for a backendRef.
      Programmed ...... condition: dataplane/LB is actually configured & live.
      ResolvedRefs .... condition: all referenced objects exist & are allowed.
      GAMMA ........... initiative extending Gateway API to east-west/mesh.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  🔧 DEEPER / UNDER-THE-HOOD
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    - CRD-based, not core: the API server knows nothing about Gateways until
      you `kubectl apply` the standard or experimental CRD bundle AND run a
      controller. `kubectl get gatewayclass` returning "No resources" usually
      means no controller is installed, not that you typed it wrong.
    - The data plane is the controller's choice: NGINX Gateway Fabric runs
      NGINX pods; Istio/Cilium program Envoy/eBPF; a cloud GatewayClass may
      provision a real cloud L7 load balancer. The SAME HTTPRoute YAML drives
      all of them — that portability is the headline feature.
    - Two-way handshake: a Route attaches (parentRefs) AND a Gateway allows
      (allowedRoutes). Neither side alone is enough; attachedRoutes on the
      listener status tells you if the handshake succeeded.
    - Policy attachment (future/extension): BackendTLSPolicy,
      HTTPRoute timeouts/retries, and *Policy CRDs extend behaviour without
      bloating the core spec — the explicit anti-annotation design.
    - GAMMA: the same *Route kinds, with parentRefs pointing at a Service
      instead of a Gateway, express service-mesh (east-west) routing —
      unifying ingress and mesh under one API.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  🔑 KEY TAKEAWAYS
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    🔑 Three layers: GatewayClass (cluster) ▸ Gateway (ns, listeners/TLS) ▸
       HTTPRoute (ns, paths/backends). Routes point UP via parentRefs.
    🔑 Gateway API is the role-oriented, portable SUCCESSOR to the frozen
       Ingress; it is CRD-based and needs a controller.
    🔑 Debug by reading CONDITIONS: Gateway Accepted+Programmed, listener
       ResolvedRefs, HTTPRoute Accepted+ResolvedRefs.
    🔑 Cross-namespace needs BOTH allowedRoutes (route->gateway) AND a
       ReferenceGrant (route->backend / gateway->Secret).
    🔑 Header routing and weighted splitting are FIRST-CLASS fields, not
       annotations; weights are relative ratios.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ⚠️ GOTCHAS
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ⚠️ No controller installed → Gateways stay Programmed=False with no
       address; routes go nowhere. CRDs alone do nothing.
    ⚠️ allowedRoutes defaults to "Same" namespace on many setups — a route in
       another namespace silently won't attach (NotAllowedByListeners).
    ⚠️ Cross-ns backendRef without ReferenceGrant → ResolvedRefs=False
       (RefNotPermitted); route looks Accepted but serves nothing.
    ⚠️ TLSRoute/TCPRoute/UDPRoute are v1alpha2 — not all controllers support
       them; don't assume portability for L4.
    ⚠️ Listener hostname vs route hostname mismatch → NoMatchingListener
       Hostname; the route attaches to nothing.
    ⚠️ certificateRefs Secret in another namespace also needs a ReferenceGrant.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ⚡ SPEED TIPS
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ⚡ Start debugging at the HTTPRoute (`describe`), not the Gateway — its
       parents[].conditions tell you immediately if attachment failed and why.
    ⚡ `kubectl get gateway -A` and check the Programmed column / ADDRESS first.
    ⚡ Reach for `kubectl explain httproute.spec...` instead of memorising the
       nested schema (matches/filters/backendRefs).
    ⚡ One Gateway + TLS owned by platform, many routes by app teams — copy an
       existing HTTPRoute and just change hostnames/paths/backendRefs.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  🔑 COMMANDS (quick recall)
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    kubectl get gatewayclass,gateway,httproute -A
    kubectl describe httproute <name> -n <ns>     # conditions first
    kubectl describe gateway <name> -n <ns>       # listeners/Programmed
    kubectl get gateway <name> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[0].value}'
    kubectl api-resources --api-group=gateway.networking.k8s.io
    kubectl explain httproute.spec.rules

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  🧪 LAB Q&A
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    🧪 Q1 (🟢) Which resource does the APPLICATION (jobpost) team create to
       route /jobs to its Service, and which field attaches it to the
       platform team's Gateway?
       A1: An HTTPRoute; the spec.parentRefs field (with the Gateway name,
       its namespace, and optionally sectionName for the listener) attaches
       it. backendRefs points at jobpost-svc:8000.

    🧪 Q2 (🟡) `kubectl describe httproute jobpost-route` shows
       Accepted=True but ResolvedRefs=False with reason BackendNotFound.
       What is wrong and where do you fix it?
       A2: The backendRefs target a Service that doesn't exist or has a wrong
       name/port. Fix the Route's spec.rules[].backendRefs (name/port) — the
       Gateway accepted the route, the backend just isn't resolvable.

    🧪 Q3 (🟡) You need a 90/10 canary between jobpost-svc and jobpost-canary.
       Write the rule fragment and state how weights are interpreted.
       A3:
         rules:
           - backendRefs:
               - { name: jobpost-svc,    port: 8000, weight: 90 }
               - { name: jobpost-canary, port: 8000, weight: 10 }
       Weights are RELATIVE ratios (90:10 == 9:1), not strict percentages.

    🧪 Q4 (🔴) An HTTPRoute in ns "jobpost" references a Service "billing-svc"
       in ns "payments". It is Accepted but no traffic flows; ResolvedRefs is
       False (RefNotPermitted). What must be created and where?
       A4: A ReferenceGrant in the TARGET namespace (payments) with
       from: {kind: HTTPRoute, namespace: jobpost} and to: {kind: Service,
       name: billing-svc}. Cross-namespace references require the referenced
       object's owner to opt in.

    🧪 Q5 (🟡) Translate this Ingress idea to Gateway API: host
       easypj.example.com, path /jobs (Prefix) -> jobpost-svc:8000, with TLS
       from Secret easypj-tls. Which fields go on the Gateway vs the HTTPRoute?
       A5: On the GATEWAY: a listener protocol HTTPS, port 443, tls.mode
       Terminate, certificateRefs -> Secret easypj-tls, and gatewayClassName.
       On the HTTPRoute: hostnames [easypj.example.com], rules[].matches path
       PathPrefix /jobs, backendRefs jobpost-svc:8000, and parentRefs to the
       Gateway's https listener.

    🧪 Q6 (🟢) `kubectl get gatewayclass` returns "No resources found" right
       after applying the Gateway API CRDs. Is this an error? Why?
       A6: Not by itself — CRDs only add the resource types. A GatewayClass is
       created by an installed CONTROLLER (Istio, Cilium, NGINX Gateway
       Fabric, Contour). No controller → no GatewayClass → Gateways stay
       Programmed=False with no address. Install a controller.


==============================================================================
  Appendix K: Helm & Kustomize Reference
==============================================================================
  Helm: chart layout, lifecycle commands, values precedence, hooks. Kustomize:
  kustomization.yaml fields, patches, generators, components, overlays.

  META: Reference appendix | Difficulty 🟡 | Both Helm and Kustomize are valid
        ways to template/manage the easypj manifests across dev/stage/prod.
  WHY THIS MATTERS: Raw YAML duplicates config across environments. Helm
        packages it as a versioned, parameterized chart; Kustomize layers
        overlays on a shared base. The CKA exam ships with Kustomize built into
        kubectl (`kubectl apply -k`) and Helm available as a separate binary.

  🧭 DECISION GUIDE — Helm vs Kustomize
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Need...                          │  Use Helm   │  Use Kustomize      │
    ├───────────────────────────────────┼─────────────┼─────────────────────┤
    │  Package & share with others      │     ✔       │   (raw dirs only)   │
    │  Versioned releases + rollback    │     ✔       │        ✘            │
    │  Conditionals / loops / functions │     ✔ (Go)  │        ✘            │
    │  Install third-party app          │     ✔       │   (if it ships base)│
    │  Template-free, pure YAML         │     ✘       │        ✔            │
    │  Built into kubectl (no binary)   │     ✘       │   ✔ (apply -k)      │
    │  Simple env overlays (dev/prod)   │   ✔ values  │   ✔ overlays        │
    │  GitOps-friendly diffable output  │   (helm     │   ✔ (kustomize      │
    │                                   │    template)│       build)        │
    └───────────────────────────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────────────┘
    💡 They COMPOSE: `helm template | kustomize` or use Kustomize's helmCharts
       field to post-process a rendered Helm chart.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PART 1 — HELM
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  📖 KEY TERMS
    Chart      A package of templated Kubernetes manifests + metadata.
    Release    A specific install of a chart into a cluster (named instance).
    Repository A server hosting packaged charts (index.yaml + .tgz files).
    Values     User-supplied parameters that fill in the templates.
    Revision   A numbered snapshot of a release; rollback targets a revision.

  🧪 CHART DIRECTORY LAYOUT
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  easypj/                            ← chart root (the chart name)     │
    │  ├── Chart.yaml                     ← metadata (name, version, deps)  │
    │  ├── values.yaml                    ← DEFAULT parameter values        │
    │  ├── values.schema.json             ← (optional) JSON-schema validate │
    │  ├── charts/                        ← bundled/subcharts (deps)        │
    │  ├── crds/                          ← CRDs installed before templates │
    │  ├── templates/                                                       │
    │  │   ├── _helpers.tpl               ← named template helpers          │
    │  │   ├── deployment.yaml            ← easypj web Deployment           │
    │  │   ├── service.yaml               ← easypj Service                  │
    │  │   ├── ingress.yaml                                                 │
    │  │   ├── configmap.yaml                                               │
    │  │   ├── secret.yaml                                                  │
    │  │   ├── hpa.yaml                                                     │
    │  │   ├── serviceaccount.yaml                                          │
    │  │   ├── NOTES.txt                  ← post-install message (templated)│
    │  │   └── tests/                                                       │
    │  │       └── test-connection.yaml   ← `helm test` pod                 │
    │  ├── .helmignore                    ← files to exclude from package   │
    │  └── README.md                                                        │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  📖 Chart.yaml FIELDS
    ┌──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Field           │  Meaning                                          │
    ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │  apiVersion      │  v2 (Helm 3). v1 is legacy Helm 2.                │
    │  name            │  Chart name (easypj).                             │
    │  version         │  SemVer of the CHART itself (e.g. 1.4.2).         │
    │  appVersion      │  Version of the app shipped (e.g. "5.2.5").       │
    │  type            │  application (default) or library.                │
    │  description     │  One-line summary.                                │
    │  kubeVersion     │  Compatible cluster range, e.g. ">=1.27.0".       │
    │  dependencies    │  List of subcharts: name, version, repository,    │
    │                  │  condition, alias, tags.                          │
    │  keywords/home/  │  Discovery metadata.                              │
    │   sources/icon   │                                                   │
    │  maintainers     │  name/email/url list.                             │
    └──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  🔑 HELM LIFECYCLE COMMANDS
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  CREATE / PACKAGE                                                     │
    │    helm create easypj                # scaffold a new chart          │
    │    helm lint easypj/                 # static-check the chart        │
    │    helm package easypj/              # build easypj-1.4.2.tgz        │
    │    helm dependency update easypj/    # pull subcharts into charts/   │
    │    helm dependency build easypj/     # rebuild from Chart.lock       │
    │                                                                      │
    │  RENDER / INSPECT (no cluster writes)                                │
    │    helm template easypj ./easypj     # render manifests to stdout    │
    │    helm template easypj ./easypj --debug                            │
    │    helm show values ./easypj         # print default values.yaml    │
    │    helm show chart ./easypj          # print Chart.yaml              │
    │    helm get manifest easypj          # rendered manifest of release  │
    │    helm get values easypj            # values used by a release      │
    │                                                                      │
    │  INSTALL / UPGRADE                                                   │
    │    helm install easypj ./easypj -n jobs --create-namespace          │
    │    helm install easypj ./easypj -f prod-values.yaml                 │
    │    helm install easypj ./easypj --set image.tag=5.2.5              │
    │    helm install easypj ./easypj --dry-run --debug                   │
    │    helm upgrade easypj ./easypj -f prod-values.yaml                 │
    │    helm upgrade --install easypj ./easypj   # idempotent (CI)        │
    │    helm upgrade easypj ./easypj --atomic --timeout 5m               │
    │      (--atomic = auto-rollback if the upgrade fails)                 │
    │                                                                      │
    │  RELEASE STATE / HISTORY / ROLLBACK                                  │
    │    helm list -n jobs                 # releases in a namespace        │
    │    helm list -A                      # all namespaces                 │
    │    helm status easypj                                                │
    │    helm history easypj               # revision list                  │
    │    helm rollback easypj 3            # revert to revision 3           │
    │    helm rollback easypj             # roll back to previous revision │
    │                                                                      │
    │  TEST / UNINSTALL                                                    │
    │    helm test easypj                  # run templates/tests/ pods      │
    │    helm uninstall easypj -n jobs                                     │
    │    helm uninstall easypj --keep-history                              │
    │                                                                      │
    │  REPOSITORIES                                                        │
    │    helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami          │
    │    helm repo update                                                  │
    │    helm repo list                                                    │
    │    helm search repo postgres                                        │
    │    helm search hub wordpress                                        │
    │    helm pull bitnami/postgresql --untar                              │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  🔧 VALUES PRECEDENCE (lowest → highest; later overrides earlier)
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  1. Chart's own values.yaml          (the defaults)                  │
    │  2. Parent chart values for subchart  (parent overrides child)       │
    │  3. -f / --values file(s)             (applied in the order given)   │
    │  4. --set / --set-string / --set-file (CLI; beats every file)        │
    │                                                                      │
    │     values.yaml  <  -f a.yaml  <  -f b.yaml  <  --set key=val        │
    │     (right-most wins on conflict)                                     │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ⚠️ GOTCHA: multiple -f files MERGE (deep); --set with a list REPLACES
       the whole list, it does not append. Use --set-string to force a value
       like "5.2.5" to stay a string, not a number.

  📖 TEMPLATE SYNTAX QUICK REFERENCE (Go text/template + Sprig)
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  {{ .Values.image.tag }}            value from values.yaml           │
    │  {{ .Release.Name }}                release name (easypj)            │
    │  {{ .Release.Namespace }}           target namespace                 │
    │  {{ .Chart.Name }} / .Chart.Version chart metadata                   │
    │  {{ .Capabilities.KubeVersion }}    cluster version info             │
    │  {{ .Files.Get "config.ini" }}      read a file from the chart       │
    │  {{ include "easypj.labels" . }}    call a named template (_helpers) │
    │  {{ tpl .Values.cfg . }}            render a string as a template    │
    │  {{- if .Values.ingress.enabled }}  conditional (the - trims space)  │
    │  {{- range .Values.env }} … {{- end}}  loop                          │
    │  {{ .Values.x | default "web" | quote }}  pipeline + Sprig funcs     │
    │  {{ required "tag is required" .Values.image.tag }}  hard-fail guard │
    │  {{ toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 12 }}  emit a YAML sub-tree   │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  🔧 HELM HOOKS (lifecycle extension points)
    Declared via the annotation  "helm.sh/hook": <event>  on a resource.
    ┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Hook event          │  Fires...                                     │
    ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │  pre-install         │  after templates render, before any create    │
    │  post-install        │  after all resources are created              │
    │  pre-upgrade         │  before an upgrade applies                     │
    │  post-upgrade        │  after an upgrade applies                      │
    │  pre-rollback        │  before a rollback applies                     │
    │  post-rollback       │  after a rollback applies                      │
    │  pre-delete          │  before any resource is deleted                │
    │  post-delete         │  after all resources are deleted               │
    │  test                │  on `helm test` (the test pods)               │
    └──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    Supporting annotations:
      "helm.sh/hook-weight": "5"          execution order (low → high)
      "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy":        before-hook-creation |
                                           hook-succeeded | hook-failed
    💡 Classic use: a pre-upgrade Job that runs `python manage.py migrate`
       for easypj before the new Deployment rolls out.

      Example easypj DB-migration hook (templates/migrate-job.yaml):
      ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │  apiVersion: batch/v1                                              │
      │  kind: Job                                                         │
      │  metadata:                                                         │
      │    name: {{ .Release.Name }}-migrate                              │
      │    annotations:                                                    │
      │      "helm.sh/hook": pre-upgrade,pre-install                       │
      │      "helm.sh/hook-weight": "-1"                                   │
      │      "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation            │
      │  spec:                                                             │
      │    template:                                                       │
      │      spec:                                                         │
      │        restartPolicy: Never                                       │
      │        containers:                                                │
      │        - name: migrate                                            │
      │          image: easypj:{{ .Values.image.tag }}                    │
      │          command: ["python","manage.py","migrate","--noinput"]    │
      └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PART 2 — KUSTOMIZE
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  📖 KEY TERMS
    Base        A directory with a kustomization.yaml + the common resources.
    Overlay     A directory that references a base and patches it per-env.
    Patch       A surgical change applied to a resource (strategic or JSON6902).
    Generator   Produces ConfigMaps/Secrets from files/literals (with hash).
    Component   Reusable, optional kustomization fragment included by overlays.

  🧪 OVERLAY DIRECTORY LAYOUT (easypj)
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  easypj/                                                             │
    │  ├── base/                                                           │
    │  │   ├── kustomization.yaml                                          │
    │  │   ├── deployment.yaml         ← easypj web Deployment             │
    │  │   ├── service.yaml                                                │
    │  │   ├── configmap.yaml                                              │
    │  │   └── ingress.yaml                                                │
    │  ├── components/                                                     │
    │  │   └── postgres/                ← optional add-on                  │
    │  │       └── kustomization.yaml                                      │
    │  └── overlays/                                                       │
    │      ├── dev/                                                        │
    │      │   ├── kustomization.yaml   ← resources: ../../base            │
    │      │   └── replica-patch.yaml                                      │
    │      ├── staging/                                                    │
    │      │   └── kustomization.yaml                                      │
    │      └── prod/                                                       │
    │          ├── kustomization.yaml                                      │
    │          ├── replica-patch.yaml   ← bump replicas to 4              │
    │          └── resources-patch.yaml ← raise CPU/mem limits           │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  📖 kustomization.yaml FIELDS
    ┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Field               │  Purpose                                      │
    ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │  apiVersion/kind     │  kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 / Kustomization│
    │  resources           │  files or dirs (bases) to include             │
    │  namespace           │  set namespace on every resource              │
    │  namePrefix /        │  prepend/append to every resource name        │
    │   nameSuffix         │                                               │
    │  commonLabels /      │  add labels to all resources (& selectors)    │
    │   labels             │  labels: can opt out of selector mutation     │
    │  commonAnnotations   │  add annotations to all resources             │
    │  images              │  override image name/newTag/newName/digest    │
    │  replicas            │  override replica count by name               │
    │  patches             │  strategic-merge OR JSON6902 patches          │
    │  patchesStrategicMerge  (legacy) merge-patch file list               │
    │  patchesJson6902        (legacy) op-based patch list                 │
    │  configMapGenerator  │  build ConfigMaps from literals/files/env      │
    │  secretGenerator     │  build Secrets (base64) from literals/files    │
    │  generatorOptions    │  disableNameSuffixHash, labels, annotations    │
    │  components          │  include reusable Component kustomizations     │
    │  vars / replacements │  substitute fields across resources           │
    │  configurations      │  custom transformer config (extra fields)     │
    │  openapi             │  schema for unknown CRDs                       │
    └──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  🔑 KUSTOMIZE COMMANDS
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  kubectl kustomize overlays/prod         # render to stdout           │
    │  kubectl apply -k overlays/prod          # render + apply             │
    │  kubectl delete -k overlays/prod                                     │
    │  kubectl diff -k overlays/prod                                       │
    │                                                                      │
    │  (standalone binary — newer features than the bundled kubectl one)   │
    │  kustomize build overlays/prod                                       │
    │  kustomize build overlays/prod | kubectl apply -f -                  │
    │  kustomize create --autodetect          # scaffold a kustomization   │
    │  kustomize edit set image easypj=easypj:5.2.5                        │
    │  kustomize edit add resource deployment.yaml                         │
    │  kustomize edit set namespace jobs                                   │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ⚠️ GOTCHA: `kubectl`'s embedded Kustomize lags the standalone `kustomize`
       binary. If a field (e.g. `components`, `replacements`) errors under
       `kubectl apply -k`, render with the standalone binary and pipe it in.

  🔧 PATCH TYPES
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  STRATEGIC-MERGE PATCH (looks like a partial resource)               │
    │    # overlays/prod/replica-patch.yaml                                │
    │    apiVersion: apps/v1                                               │
    │    kind: Deployment                                                  │
    │    metadata:                                                         │
    │      name: easypj-web                                                │
    │    spec:                                                             │
    │      replicas: 4              ← merged onto the base                 │
    │                                                                      │
    │  JSON6902 PATCH (explicit op/path/value)                            │
    │    patches:                                                          │
    │    - target:                                                        │
    │        kind: Deployment                                             │
    │        name: easypj-web                                             │
    │      patch: |-                                                      │
    │        - op: replace                                                │
    │          path: /spec/replicas                                       │
    │          value: 4                                                   │
    │        - op: add                                                    │
    │          path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-              │
    │          value: {name: DJANGO_DEBUG, value: "0"}                    │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    💡 op verbs: add | remove | replace | move | copy | test.
       `/-` at the end of a path means "append to this list".

  🔧 GENERATORS (ConfigMap / Secret)
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  configMapGenerator:                                                 │
    │  - name: easypj-config                                               │
    │    literals:                                                         │
    │    - DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=easypj.settings.prod                     │
    │    - ALLOWED_HOSTS=jobs.example.com                                  │
    │    files:                                                            │
    │    - gunicorn.conf.py                                                │
    │  secretGenerator:                                                    │
    │  - name: easypj-secret                                               │
    │    literals:                                                         │
    │    - DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=changeme                                      │
    │    envs:                                                             │
    │    - db.env                                                          │
    │  generatorOptions:                                                   │
    │    disableNameSuffixHash: false   ← keep the content hash suffix     │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    🔧 UNDER-THE-HOOD: generators append a hash to the name
       (easypj-config-7t4m9k2bd6). Editing the data changes the hash, which
       changes every reference, which forces a rolling Deployment update —
       config changes can't be silently ignored. Set disableNameSuffixHash:
       true only when an external resource references the fixed name.

  📖 COMPONENTS (reusable optional fragments)
    A Component is like a base but uses kind: Component and is pulled in via
    the `components:` field, so several overlays can opt into the same add-on.
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  # components/postgres/kustomization.yaml                            │
    │  apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1                        │
    │  kind: Component                                                     │
    │  resources:                                                          │
    │  - statefulset.yaml                                                  │
    │  - service.yaml                                                      │
    │  secretGenerator:                                                    │
    │  - name: pg-secret                                                   │
    │    literals: [POSTGRES_PASSWORD=changeme]                            │
    │                                                                      │
    │  # overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml                                  │
    │  resources:                                                          │
    │  - ../../base                                                        │
    │  components:                                                         │
    │  - ../../components/postgres                                         │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  🧠 ANALOGY: Helm is a cake MIX (parameterized recipe you ship in a box and
     bake with your own values); Kustomize is taking a plain cake (the base)
     and adding frosting layers (overlays) without rewriting the recipe.

  🔑 KEY TAKEAWAYS
    • Helm = packaging + versioned releases + rollback + templating.
    • Kustomize = template-free overlays, built into `kubectl apply -k`.
    • Helm values precedence: values.yaml < -f files (in order) < --set.
    • `--atomic` auto-rolls-back a failed Helm upgrade; `helm rollback N`
      reverts to a revision.
    • Kustomize generators hash content → editing config forces a rollout.
    • Use `helm template` / `kustomize build` to diff before applying (GitOps).

  ⚠️ GOTCHAS
    • `helm install` fails if the release name already exists — use
      `helm upgrade --install` for idempotency.
    • `--set list[0]=x` REPLACES lists, never appends; deep-merge only via -f.
    • kubectl's built-in Kustomize is older than the standalone binary.
    • A secretGenerator stores values base64-only — NOT encrypted at rest.
    • Helm CRDs in crds/ are installed once and NOT upgraded/deleted by Helm.

  ⚡ SPEED TIPS
    • `helm upgrade --install easypj ./easypj -f prod.yaml --atomic` is the
      one-liner CI deploy.
    • `kubectl apply -k overlays/prod` needs no extra binary in the exam.
    • `helm template … | kubectl apply -f -` works even where Tiller-less
      RBAC blocks a direct install.
    • `kustomize edit set image easypj=easypj:NEWTAG` bumps the tag without
      hand-editing YAML.

  🔑 COMMANDS (cheat block)
    helm create / lint / package / template / install / upgrade / rollback
    helm upgrade --install NAME ./chart -f vals.yaml --atomic
    helm history NAME ; helm get values NAME ; helm get manifest NAME
    kubectl kustomize DIR ; kubectl apply -k DIR ; kubectl diff -k DIR
    kustomize build DIR | kubectl apply -f -
    kustomize edit set image NAME=IMG:TAG ; kustomize edit set namespace NS

  🧪 LAB Q&A
    Q1. easypj is installed as a Helm release; the new image crashes on
        startup. How do you revert without re-rendering YAML?
      A. `helm history easypj` to find the last good revision, then
         `helm rollback easypj <N>`. Or upgrade with `--atomic` next time so
         a failed rollout self-reverts.
    Q2. Two values files plus a --set flag set the same image.tag. Which wins?
      A. --set wins. Order is values.yaml < -f file1 < -f file2 < --set.
    Q3. You edit a Kustomize configMapGenerator literal but the running Pods
        keep the old value. Why might they NOT, and what guarantees a refresh?
      A. By default the generated ConfigMap name carries a content hash, so
         editing it changes the name and triggers a rolling update. If
         disableNameSuffixHash: true is set, the name is fixed and Pods won't
         restart — re-enable the hash or trigger a rollout restart.
    Q4. The exam terminal has kubectl but no helm binary, and you must apply
        the easypj prod overlay. Command?
      A. `kubectl apply -k overlays/prod` (Kustomize is built into kubectl).
    Q5. You need to run `manage.py migrate` for easypj before each Helm
        upgrade rolls the new Deployment. How?
      A. Add a Job annotated `"helm.sh/hook": pre-upgrade` (with a negative
         hook-weight) running the migrate command, plus a
         hook-delete-policy of before-hook-creation.
    Q6. `helm install easypj ./easypj` errors "cannot re-use a name that is
        still in use." How do you make the deploy idempotent for CI?
      A. Use `helm upgrade --install easypj ./easypj` — it installs if absent,
         upgrades if present.


  Appendix L: The Imperative Command Generator (cheat sheet)
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Every "create X fast" one-liner + the $do pattern to scaffold YAML you then
    edit — the single biggest exam time-saver, grouped by resource.

    💡 insight — In the exam you are graded on the RESULT, not on how you got
      there. Typing a 40-line Pod manifest by hand wastes minutes you do not
      have. The fastest path is almost always: run an imperative `kubectl
      create/run` with `--dry-run=client -o yaml` to SCAFFOLD a manifest, pipe
      it to a file, then open it in vim and edit only the few fields the
      imperative form cannot express. This appendix is that scaffold, end to
      end.


    L.1 — THE TWO ALIASES THAT POWER EVERYTHING
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Put these in your shell the FIRST minute of the exam (also App A.9, Ch 45.1):

      alias k=kubectl
      export do='--dry-run=client -o yaml'      # "dry output"
      export now='--force --grace-period=0'     # "delete now"

    🔑 must-remember — With these set, the universal scaffold pattern is:

      k create <resource> <name> [flags] $do > res.yaml
      vim res.yaml            # edit the bits imperative cannot set
      k apply -f res.yaml

    ⚠️ gotcha — `--dry-run=client` (validates locally, prints YAML, contacts
      no API objects) is what you want for scaffolding. `--dry-run=server`
      actually runs admission/defaulting on the server (use it to TEST whether
      a create would be accepted). Plain `--dry-run` (no value) is removed.

      ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │  IMPERATIVE  →  YAML  →  EDIT  →  APPLY      (the exam time-saver loop) │
      │                                                                        │
      │   k run web --image=nginx $do  ──▶  pod.yaml  ──▶  vim  ──▶  k apply    │
      │      └ scaffolds in <1s            └ valid skeleton   └ tweak  └ live   │
      └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


    L.2 — WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE MADE IMPERATIVELY
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    🧭 decision guide — `kubectl create` has a SUBCOMMAND only for a fixed set
      of resources. `kubectl run` makes a Pod. Everything else you scaffold from
      the closest one (or App B template), then edit.

      ┌────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ Has its own create verb     │ create deployment / service / configmap /│
      │ (scaffold directly)         │ secret / job / cronjob / namespace /     │
      │                             │ serviceaccount / role / rolebinding /    │
      │                             │ clusterrole / clusterrolebinding /       │
      │                             │ quota / priorityclass / poddisruption-   │
      │                             │ budget / ingress / token                 │
      ├────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
      │ Pod                         │ kubectl run (NOT create pod)             │
      ├────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
      │ No create verb — scaffold   │ StatefulSet, DaemonSet, PV, PVC, Storage-│
      │ from nearest + edit, or use │ Class, NetworkPolicy, HPA(*), CRD, Gate- │
      │ App B template              │ way/HTTPRoute  (*HPA: `autoscale` verb)  │
      └────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘


    L.3 — PODS  (kubectl run)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # bare pod
      k run nginx --image=nginx

      # scaffold a pod manifest to edit
      k run nginx --image=nginx $do > pod.yaml

      # pod with a command + args (note the -- separator)
      k run busybox --image=busybox --command -- sleep 3600
      k run busybox --image=busybox $do -- /bin/sh -c "echo hi && sleep 1d"

      # pod with a container port exposed
      k run web --image=nginx --port=80

      # pod + env vars / labels
      k run web --image=nginx --env="TIER=frontend" --labels="app=easypj,env=dev"

      # pod that creates a Service at the same time
      k run web --image=nginx --port=80 --expose

      # one-shot debug pod, auto-deleted on exit
      k run tmp --image=busybox --rm -it --restart=Never -- sh

      # easypj app smoke-test pod hitting the jobpost endpoint
      k run curl --image=curlimages/curl --rm -it --restart=Never -- \
        curl -s http://easypj-web.default.svc.cluster.local:8000/jobs/

    ⚡ speed tip — `--restart=Never` ⇒ Pod; `--restart=OnFailure` ⇒ Job;
      `--restart=Always` (default) ⇒ in old versions a Deployment, today a Pod.
      For a clean one-off task pod always pass `--restart=Never`.


    L.4 — DEPLOYMENTS, SCALING, ROLLOUTS
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      k create deployment easypj-web --image=easypj:1.0
      k create deployment easypj-web --image=easypj:1.0 --replicas=3
      k create deployment easypj-web --image=easypj:1.0 --port=8000 $do > dep.yaml

      # scale
      k scale deployment easypj-web --replicas=5

      # update the image (records a rollout revision)
      k set image deployment/easypj-web easypj=easypj:2.0

      # rollout control
      k rollout status     deployment/easypj-web
      k rollout history    deployment/easypj-web
      k rollout undo       deployment/easypj-web
      k rollout undo       deployment/easypj-web --to-revision=2
      k rollout restart    deployment/easypj-web

      # autoscale (creates an HPA — the only imperative path to one)
      k autoscale deployment easypj-web --min=2 --max=10 --cpu-percent=70

    💡 insight — `kubectl create deployment` cannot set resource requests/limits,
      probes, volumes, or multiple containers. Scaffold with `$do`, then paste in
      those blocks from App B before `k apply`.


    L.5 — SERVICES  (expose & create)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # expose an EXISTING deployment/pod (infers the selector for you)
      k expose deployment easypj-web --port=80 --target-port=8000
      k expose deployment easypj-web --port=80 --target-port=8000 --type=NodePort
      k expose deployment easypj-web --port=80 --type=LoadBalancer --name=easypj-lb
      k expose pod web --port=80 --name=web-svc

      # create a service from scratch (no selector inferred — you set it)
      k create service clusterip easypj-web --tcp=80:8000
      k create service nodeport  easypj-web --tcp=80:8000 --node-port=30080
      k create service loadbalancer easypj-web --tcp=80:8000
      k create service externalname easypj-db --external-name=db.example.com

    ⚠️ gotcha — `expose` derives the Service `selector` from the target object's
      labels; `create service` does NOT add a selector, so its Endpoints stay
      empty until you add one (or wire manual Endpoints). Use `expose` when the
      backend already exists; use `create service` for headless/ExternalName.


    L.6 — CONFIGMAPS & SECRETS
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ConfigMap
      k create configmap easypj-cfg --from-literal=DEBUG=False
      k create configmap easypj-cfg --from-literal=DEBUG=False \
                                    --from-literal=ALLOWED_HOSTS=easypj.example.com
      k create configmap easypj-cfg --from-file=settings.env
      k create configmap easypj-cfg --from-file=conf=/path/to/django.conf
      k create configmap easypj-cfg --from-env-file=app.env

      # Secret (generic)
      k create secret generic easypj-db --from-literal=POSTGRES_PASSWORD=s3cr3t
      k create secret generic easypj-db --from-file=./pg-password.txt
      k create secret generic easypj-db --from-env-file=db.env

      # Secret (docker registry pull)
      k create secret docker-registry regcred \
        --docker-server=registry.example.com \
        --docker-username=ci --docker-password=pw --docker-email=ci@easypj.io

      # Secret (TLS)
      k create secret tls easypj-tls --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key

    🔧 under-the-hood — Secret `data` values are base64, NOT encrypted at rest by
      default. `--from-literal` base64-encodes for you. To inspect:
        k get secret easypj-db -o jsonpath='{.data.POSTGRES_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d


    L.7 — JOBS & CRONJOBS
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      k create job migrate --image=easypj:1.0 -- python manage.py migrate
      k create job migrate --image=easypj:1.0 $do -- python manage.py migrate > job.yaml

      # cronjob (schedule is the standard 5-field cron expression)
      k create cronjob reaper --image=busybox --schedule="*/5 * * * *" -- \
        /bin/sh -c "date; echo cleanup"

      # run a Job once from an existing CronJob
      k create job --from=cronjob/reaper reaper-manual

    ⚡ speed tip — For a one-shot task pod that retries, `k run x --image=...
      --restart=OnFailure` makes a Job-like Pod, but `k create job` gives you the
      proper Job object with backoffLimit/completions — prefer it on the exam.


    L.8 — NAMESPACES, QUOTAS, LIMITS, PDB, PRIORITY
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      k create namespace easypj
      k create quota dev-quota --hard=cpu=4,memory=8Gi,pods=20 -n easypj
      k create priorityclass high-prio --value=1000 --global-default=false
      k create poddisruptionbudget easypj-pdb --selector=app=easypj --min-available=2

      # LimitRange has no create verb — scaffold from App B and apply.

    🧪 lab — "give the easypj namespace a 4-CPU / 8Gi cap and keep 2 web pods up
      during disruptions":
        k create namespace easypj
        k create quota easypj-q --hard=cpu=4,memory=8Gi -n easypj
        k create pdb easypj-web-pdb --selector=app=easypj-web --min-available=2 -n easypj


    L.9 — RBAC  (the big exam earner)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # service account
      k create serviceaccount easypj-sa
      k create token easypj-sa                      # short-lived token (v1.24+)
      k create token easypj-sa --duration=1h

      # role / clusterrole  (verbs + resources, optionally resourceNames)
      k create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods
      k create role pod-rw --verb=get,list,watch,create,update,delete \
                           --resource=pods,deployments
      k create role one-cm --verb=get --resource=configmaps \
                           --resource-name=easypj-cfg
      k create clusterrole node-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=nodes
      k create clusterrole url-get --verb=get --non-resource-url=/healthz

      # bind a role/clusterrole to a user, group, or serviceaccount
      k create rolebinding pr-bind --role=pod-reader --user=jane
      k create rolebinding pr-bind --role=pod-reader \
                                   --serviceaccount=default:easypj-sa
      k create clusterrolebinding ro-all --clusterrole=view --group=dev-team

      # verify effective permissions (auth can-i)
      k auth can-i list pods --as=jane
      k auth can-i '*' '*' --as=system:serviceaccount:default:easypj-sa

      ┌──────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
      │ Scope        │ Role object          │ Binding object                   │
      ├──────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
      │ one namespace│ Role                 │ RoleBinding                      │
      │ whole cluster│ ClusterRole          │ ClusterRoleBinding               │
      │ cluster role,│ ClusterRole          │ RoleBinding   (grants only in    │
      │   one ns     │   (reused)           │   that one namespace)            │
      └──────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘

    🔑 must-remember — `--role` ⇒ RoleBinding; `--clusterrole` ⇒ may go in either
      a RoleBinding (namespaced grant) or ClusterRoleBinding (cluster-wide grant).


    L.10 — INGRESS  (and the Gateway API note)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      k create ingress easypj-ing \
        --rule="easypj.example.com/jobs*=easypj-web:80" \
        --rule="easypj.example.com/skills*=easypj-web:80"
      k create ingress easypj-ing --class=nginx \
        --rule="easypj.example.com/*=easypj-web:80,tls=easypj-tls" $do > ing.yaml

    🏢 beyond — Gateway API (Gateway / HTTPRoute, Ch 20b, App J) has NO `kubectl
      create` verb — scaffold from the App J / App B template and `k apply`.


    L.11 — ANNOTATE, LABEL, TAINT, CORDON  (mutate fast, no YAML)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      k label pod web tier=frontend
      k label pod web tier=backend --overwrite
      k label pod web tier-                         # remove a label
      k annotate pod web description="easypj front end"
      k annotate svc easypj-web prometheus.io/scrape=true

      # node scheduling controls
      k taint node node1 key=value:NoSchedule
      k taint node node1 key=value:NoSchedule-       # remove taint
      k cordon   node1                               # mark unschedulable
      k uncordon node1
      k drain    node1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data


    L.12 — PATCH & SET  (surgical edits without opening an editor)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # strategic-merge patch (default)
      k patch deployment easypj-web -p '{"spec":{"replicas":4}}'

      # json patch (precise, index-addressed)
      k patch deployment easypj-web --type=json \
        -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":6}]'

      # set helpers
      k set image deployment/easypj-web easypj=easypj:2.0
      k set env  deployment/easypj-web DEBUG=False
      k set resources deployment/easypj-web \
        --limits=cpu=500m,memory=256Mi --requests=cpu=100m,memory=128Mi
      k set serviceaccount deployment/easypj-web easypj-sa


    L.13 — INSPECT, EXPLAIN & WAIT  (verify what you generated)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      k explain pod.spec.containers          # field docs, no internet needed
      k explain deploy --recursive | less    # the whole tree of fields
      k get pod web -o yaml                   # the live object
      k get pod web -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}'
      k get pods -o wide --show-labels
      k diff -f dep.yaml                       # what would change before apply
      k wait --for=condition=Ready pod/web --timeout=60s
      k wait --for=condition=Available deploy/easypj-web --timeout=120s

    💡 insight — `k explain` is your offline manual in the exam. When you forget
      the path to readinessProbe or a tolerations field, `k explain
      pod.spec.containers.readinessProbe` answers in one line.


    L.14 — THE ONE-PAGE LOOKUP TABLE
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ┌────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ I need…            │ Fastest command                                  │
      ├────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
      │ a Pod              │ k run NAME --image=IMG $do > p.yaml              │
      │ a Deployment       │ k create deploy NAME --image=IMG --replicas=N $do │
      │ a Service (exists) │ k expose deploy NAME --port=80 --target-port=8000 │
      │ a Service (new)    │ k create service clusterip NAME --tcp=80:8000    │
      │ a ConfigMap        │ k create cm NAME --from-literal=K=V              │
      │ a Secret           │ k create secret generic NAME --from-literal=K=V  │
      │ a Job              │ k create job NAME --image=IMG -- CMD             │
      │ a CronJob          │ k create cronjob NAME --image=IMG --schedule="…" │
      │ a Namespace        │ k create ns NAME                                 │
      │ a ResourceQuota    │ k create quota NAME --hard=cpu=4,memory=8Gi      │
      │ a PDB              │ k create pdb NAME --selector=… --min-available=2 │
      │ a ServiceAccount   │ k create sa NAME                                 │
      │ a Role             │ k create role NAME --verb=get,list --resource=po │
      │ a RoleBinding      │ k create rolebinding NAME --role=R --user=U      │
      │ a ClusterRole      │ k create clusterrole NAME --verb=… --resource=…  │
      │ a CRB              │ k create clusterrolebinding NAME --clusterrole=…  │
      │ an Ingress         │ k create ingress NAME --rule="host/path=svc:port"│
      │ an HPA             │ k autoscale deploy NAME --min=2 --max=10 --cpu=70 │
      │ a Token            │ k create token SA                                │
      │ scale something    │ k scale deploy NAME --replicas=N                 │
      │ change an image    │ k set image deploy/NAME C=IMG:TAG                │
      │ roll back          │ k rollout undo deploy/NAME [--to-revision=R]     │
      │ a quick debug shell│ k run tmp --image=busybox --rm -it --restart=Never│
      └────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    🔑 COMMANDS — the eight to burn into muscle memory
      1. export do='--dry-run=client -o yaml'        (the scaffold flag)
      2. k run NAME --image=IMG $do > p.yaml          (any Pod, then edit)
      3. k create deploy NAME --image=IMG --replicas=N $do > d.yaml
      4. k expose deploy NAME --port=80 --target-port=PORT
      5. k create cm/secret NAME --from-literal=K=V    (config in one line)
      6. k create role+rolebinding (--verb/--resource ; --role/--user)  (RBAC)
      7. k set image / k scale / k rollout undo        (mutate live, no YAML)
      8. k explain RES.field  +  k wait --for=condition=…   (verify it worked)

    ⚠️ GOTCHAS — the slips that cost marks
      • Forgetting `=client` after `--dry-run` (server form mutates intent /
        runs admission; plain `--dry-run` is gone).
      • `k create pod` does NOT exist — it is `k run`.
      • `create service` adds NO selector ⇒ empty Endpoints; use `expose` for an
        existing backend.
      • `create deployment` cannot set probes/limits/volumes — scaffold + edit.
      • `--` must precede a container command/args, and `--command` makes it the
        entrypoint vs args.
      • RBAC `--resource-name` only narrows verbs that take a name (get/update/
        delete) — it does NOT work for list/create.

    ⚡ SPEED TIPS
      • Always pipe `$do` to a file, never hand-write a manifest from zero.
      • `k explain --recursive` beats reaching for the browser.
      • `k run ... --rm -it --restart=Never -- sh` for instant in-cluster debug.
      • `--expose` on `k run` makes Pod + Service in one shot.
      • `k create job --from=cronjob/NAME` to trigger a scheduled job on demand.

    🧪 LAB Q&A
      Q1 🟢  Make a single nginx pod named "web" without applying any YAML.
        A: k run web --image=nginx
        Why: `run` is the only imperative Pod creator; no manifest needed.

      Q2 🟢  Scaffold (don't apply) a 3-replica deployment of easypj:1.0 on
             port 8000 into dep.yaml.
        A: k create deployment easypj-web --image=easypj:1.0 --replicas=3 \
             --port=8000 --dry-run=client -o yaml > dep.yaml
        Why: `$do` validates client-side and emits YAML you then edit/apply.

      Q3 🟡  Expose an existing deployment easypj-web on port 80 → container
             8000 as a NodePort.
        A: k expose deployment easypj-web --port=80 --target-port=8000 \
             --type=NodePort
        Why: `expose` infers the selector from the deployment's pod labels;
        `--target-port` is the containerPort, `--port` is the Service port.

      Q4 🟡  Create a ConfigMap easypj-cfg with DEBUG=False and ALLOWED_HOSTS=
             easypj.example.com in one command.
        A: k create configmap easypj-cfg --from-literal=DEBUG=False \
             --from-literal=ALLOWED_HOSTS=easypj.example.com
        Why: repeat `--from-literal` per key; `--from-file`/`--from-env-file`
        for file-sourced config.

      Q5 🟡  Create a Secret easypj-db holding POSTGRES_PASSWORD=s3cr3t, then
             read it back in plaintext.
        A: k create secret generic easypj-db --from-literal=POSTGRES_PASSWORD=s3cr3t
           k get secret easypj-db -o jsonpath='{.data.POSTGRES_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d
        Why: Secret data is base64 (not encrypted by default); jsonpath +
        `base64 -d` recovers it.

      Q6 🔴  Grant user "jane" get/list/watch on pods in the default namespace,
             imperatively, then prove it.
        A: k create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods
           k create rolebinding jane-pr --role=pod-reader --user=jane
           k auth can-i list pods --as=jane        # → yes
        Why: namespaced grant = Role + RoleBinding; `--role` forces a
        RoleBinding; `auth can-i --as` confirms the effective permission.

      Q7 🔴  Give serviceaccount default:easypj-sa cluster-wide read access to
             nodes.
        A: k create clusterrole node-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=nodes
           k create clusterrolebinding sa-nodes --clusterrole=node-reader \
             --serviceaccount=default:easypj-sa
        Why: cluster-scoped resources (nodes) need a ClusterRole; binding it
        cluster-wide needs a ClusterRoleBinding.

      Q8 🟡  Update the easypj-web deployment image to easypj:2.0 and watch the
             rollout, then roll it back.
        A: k set image deployment/easypj-web easypj=easypj:2.0
           k rollout status deployment/easypj-web
           k rollout undo   deployment/easypj-web
        Why: `set image` records a revision; `rollout undo` reverts to the
        prior ReplicaSet without editing YAML.

      Q9 🟡  Create an HPA for easypj-web: 2–10 replicas at 70% CPU.
        A: k autoscale deployment easypj-web --min=2 --max=10 --cpu-percent=70
        Why: `autoscale` is the ONLY imperative way to make an HPA (there is no
        `create hpa`).

      Q10 🟢 Spin up a throwaway shell pod to curl the easypj /jobs/ endpoint
              from inside the cluster, auto-deleting on exit.
        A: k run tmp --image=curlimages/curl --rm -it --restart=Never -- \
             curl -s http://easypj-web.default.svc.cluster.local:8000/jobs/
        Why: `--rm -it --restart=Never` = interactive one-shot Pod that cleans
        itself up; perfect for service-reachability checks.

      Q11 🔴 Create a CronJob "reaper" running busybox every 5 minutes, then
              trigger it once immediately.
        A: k create cronjob reaper --image=busybox --schedule="*/5 * * * *" -- \
             /bin/sh -c "date; echo cleanup"
           k create job --from=cronjob/reaper reaper-now
        Why: `--from=cronjob/…` clones the CronJob's jobTemplate into a one-off
        Job without re-typing the spec.

      Q12 🟡 You need a manifest with a readinessProbe but forgot the field
              path. Look it up offline, then scaffold a pod to edit.
        A: k explain pod.spec.containers.readinessProbe
           k run web --image=nginx --dry-run=client -o yaml > p.yaml ; vim p.yaml
        Why: `k explain` is the in-exam offline manual; `$do` gives the editable
        skeleton you paste the probe into.

    Target Audience:   Complete Kubernetes beginners through working engineers
                       preparing for the CKA and running production clusters
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

                    — END OF THE DEFINITIVE CKA STUDY GUIDE —

         Built around the easypj / jobpost reference project. Study the
         labs, run the commands, break the cluster, then fix it. The exam
              rewards the hands that have already done the work.
